Kansas City Current's grit earns them spot in NWSL Championship while Gotham's logistics problems linger

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2250 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NEW YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches.
  • "I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune mentioned post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".
  • It has been revealed that icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NEW YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches. When the Current's Croix Bethune opened the scoring in the 20th minute with an incredible looping shot off a free kick, the theme of the day was in motion. The league would make the best of the unideal circumstances with a top-quality soccer game, or at least with a few highlight-reel moments nestled into a match contested by a collection of the world's most talented players.

"I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune mentioned post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".

It has been revealed that icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier. The Current's 2-1 win came courtesy of a chippy game plan that would have been the case if the match had taken place at a traditional soccer-specific stadium but it felt especially at home at Icahn Stadium and amidst its elements. The teams played against the wind during Newly introduced York's first properly cold weekend of the season, and Gotham faced a setting sun that impacted their vision during the first half. Bethune's impressive strike was really the only on-field spectacle to be witnessed on Randall's Island.

BEND IT LIKE BETHUNE 💫 KC takes the lead!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/F4mQePT5QJ.

"We knew it was going to be a physical game, without a doubt," Current forward Haley Hopkins remarked. "Like I said a million times, Gotham's a very, very good team and so we had to be super disciplined in our structure and catch them on their transition and we were just able to put the ball in the back of the net when we had our opportunities.".

The introduction of Gotham's Rose Lavelle, who has been dealing with niggling fitness issues over the last few weeks, did not change the smash-and-grab energy of the game. Much as there was a week ago in their quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign, there was a dull quality to Gotham's attack despite their star power. Over 180 minutes of possession play, the NWSL Shield winners managed zero shots on target and 0.66 expected goals, their midseason marquee signing Sam Kerr managing no shots along the way and mustering just one attempt in her last five matches. To say they were unlucky would be a stretch but their lively start to the second half gave their failed attempts to put a shot on frame a comedic feel.

Sources indicate that "I think we were kind of our own worst enemy today," midfielder Savannah McCaskill noted. "I think at times we played into what they wanted to do and their style of play. They want a very chippy game. They want to get into tackles. They want to draw fouls. They want to break up the game. They want to play long and that's not our style. We want to keep the ball. We want to control tempo, and we like to play pretty football. That's [what] we pride ourselves on … but I think we need to find a better way to balance that out, especially in this league. How can we meet the demand of a chippy game while also controlling the tempo? I think we did a really good job when we played them at home the last time [a 2-1 win on Aug. 14]. They scored early but then we completely dominated the rest of the game and I think we failed to do that today and so I think that's really the determining factor.".

In a recent development, in other words, it was the perfect setup for Gotham to equalize off an own goal from Laney Rouse, a week after benefiting from another own goal from the Reign's Jordyn Bugg. Those two goals would be the only ones in their postseason run, just as one might expect from the NWSL Shield winners and reigning champions who entered the playoffs as the favorites to win another title.

Gotham FC find a way to tie up the semifinal 💪NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/Itbzs4Bhz1.

Gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger then slipped into game-saving mode with two vital blocks while defender Tierna Davidson did what she could to hold the Current at bay, attempting to create a villain arc rivaled only by Argentina's run to the World Cup final. Though the hosts had lucked their way into an even game by the 88th minute, the dark and cold conditions at a downsized stadium in an obscure part of Latest York meant the game beckoned for extra time. One final smash and grab was undoubtedly in the cards, though where it would come from was hard to guess – the Current had put in the work to win but soccer's chaotic nature had already weaseled its way into the game.

Industry observers note that in the end, it was the Current's Haley Hopkins who had the final say in the 89th minute off of – what else – a set piece, a free kick that led the forward to finally evade Berger with a shot off the crossbar. After losing to them twice in three previous meetings this season, the Current earned their spot in next week's NWSL Championship (Saturday, 8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+) on the back of a well-executed gameplan.

HALEY HOPKINS CLUTCH OFF THE CROSSBAR 🤯The KC Current lead 2-1!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/BT2OZhwX1y.

"As much as we tried to analyze certain teams in the league that have given them trouble, we really took information from the games we've played against them, all the ways they challenged us," Current head coach Chris Armas mentioned. "There's been games even where they get high [expected goals], too much progression, too much in our box and we just tried to then look at all the scenes and moments when we made it hard for them so we just tried to take from yesterday and apply it to today, [that] type of thing. We gave up zero shots on goal in 90 minutes. The commitment from our players to just will themselves to it to stick to a match initiative that was going to be largely about taking away spaces, controlling the middle of the pitch and if we can do that on the day – and and we did that by running after them, too, and pressing in moments of high intensity – we not only might stop what they're trying to do on one end and maybe force the turnovers that could challenge them so a little bit of a chess match there in moments.".

Recent findings suggest that the Current were no slouches, finishing fourth in the regular season and now on a  seven-game winning streak en route to next week's championship. Bethune's star quality shone on Sunday, while the team's record with two-time NWSL MVP Temwa Chawinga and U.S. women's national team standout Michelle Cooper is formidable. It did not erase the fact that they slayed a giant along the way, knocking out the Shield winners and a team that had picked up five major titles in four seasons.

It has been revealed that "Gotham has just raised the bar around the league and in our country here, so the way they play, the way the coach sets them up, the talent on the team, the type of games they can put you in, you have to come with a plan," Armas remarked. "They're a team that, again, if iron sharpens iron type of thing, we try to push teams and we try to raise the bar.".

Gotham, though, had not looked the part of the NWSL's gold standard team. Their drastic run, while currently headlined by USWNT players Lavelle and Jaedyn Shaw, is built on the back of an effective defensive structure that has carried an inconsistent offense. Lavelle and, in particular, Shaw have picked up much of the slack en route to the NWSL Shield and Kerr was supposed to bolster their attack after Esther Gonzalez's shock departure for Saudi club Al Qadsiah. They finished the regular season sixth in the NWSL for expected goals with 49.01 but had a genuine finishing problem, notching just 39 goals and ranking in the league's bottom six in that category. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros is not sounding the alarm just yet but as they enter another offseason, the attacking composition of the team deserves yet another look.

"Of course, we want to create more chances, more shots," Amoros mentioned. "We all do but we look at the way we play. We look at the way we create chances. We look at who does that. I think when it comes to these games, could we have [made] some better decisions? Yes, we did. We actually create some good moments. Yes, I wouldn't over-think about it. Something that I'm happy [about]? No but at the same time, we work a lot to make sure that those moments happen. So you know the set pieces, those situations, the open plays, final decisions … Definitely, something that we want to be better [at]. We want to score more goals. I think that we are the best team defending in the league with our aggressive approach to defending but we want to also be able to create and score more goals.".

It has been revealed that more importantly, though, Gotham were not treated like the bar-raising team they have become over the years. Icahn Stadium has its charms and is a worthy inclusion on the list of wacky and wonderful places that embody American soccer, an enjoyably chaotic slice of the world's most popular game. It was also a back-up blueprint for a team that has called Sports Illustrated Stadium home for five years, settling in nicely to a state-of-the-art soccer-specific build for MLS' Red Bull New York that can hold 20,000 more fans than the 5,000-seater Icahn Stadium can. The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, managed by RBNY, had fallen into disrepair and with the primary tenants' end-of-season friendly scheduled for the night before, there was not enough time to fix it. The quirks of Icahn Stadium only served as a reminder that Gotham – and the NWSL – should not have actually been there, even if the field at Randall's Island was better suited for the occasion.

"I want to be really clear and direct in saying that in these types of situations, the field is never an excuse," winger Midge Purce stated. "We lost today because we weren't the better team. That being said, I would say it's inexcusable. It's not what you want in a professional league. It's not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it's a bad look for everyone involved and we always want to be at Sports Illustrated [Stadium] in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season but I would say it had no effect on performance today.".

According to recent reports, the Current's trip to Icahn Stadium is not where the NWSL's efforts to make lemonade end, either. Saturday's semifinal, in which the Washington Spirit beat the Utah Royals to book their spot in a championship game at their home of Audi Field, only added to it. One of the Spirit's sponsors underwrote the costs to push the start time of the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III football game, by a few hours but both matches were played on a field with soccer and football lines. The football lines will likely be faint but visible for next week's NWSL Championship, while the playability of the actual field will probably face a few questions in the build-up.

Industry observers note that "I think we will never know what happened if we would have played [at Sports Illustrated Stadium] on a good pitch," Amoros said. "I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable under our view. The last couple of games we picked up injuries. Luckily, nothing that has been a season-ending injury but we have to protect our players and guarantee the quality of football so to thank the club, obviously.

In a recent development, "Overall, I think it's been a sad weekend. I think also the situation in Washington yesterday. This league deserves better. The two, arguably, best teams, [most] consistent, having to deal with these situations and then yesterday, you sit down to watch that game around the world and you're seeing those American football lines across today. Credit to the club and the fans. I think they've done an amazing job here. The fans welcomed us. The club has really shifted everything to play here but we couldn't play in our ground where we could have had more people, where we are unbeaten in 13 games at the moment and but I think we took that decision, putting players' safety first, and the outcome is the outcome.".

German economy returns to growth, so why is the country still worried?

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1235 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that is Germany's economy back on the up?
  • Sources indicate that at the 2026 Mechanical Engineering Summit in Berlin this week, the mood was sullen.
  • Sources indicate that the mechanical and plant engineering sector was the backbone of German industry for decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that is Germany's economy back on the up? The answer to that question depends on your perspective.

Sources indicate that at the 2026 Mechanical Engineering Summit in Berlin this week, the mood was sullen. "A year ago, I mentioned here: We are angry. Today I must say: We are stunned," Bertram Kawlath, president of the Mechanical Engineering Industry Association (VDMA), said in his opening remarks on Tuesday.

Sources indicate that the mechanical and plant engineering sector was the backbone of German industry for decades. It once employed more than a million people; now 15,000 positions are being cut every month. Production has shrunk about 20% since 2018.

Kawlath criticized the federal government's infighting and lack of reform, as well as what the companies consider a continued high bureaucracy and tax burden.

"[We are] stunned by the whitewashing in so many government statements. Stunned by the increasingly visible decline of our country as a business location.".

It has been revealed that german Chancellor Friedrich Merz promised quick reforms and a rapidly noticeable economic upswing when he took office in May 2025. A year and a half later, reality has caught up with him.

Sources indicate that merz's coalition of his conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), its Bavarian sister party the Christian Social Union, (CSU), along with the center-left Social Democrats(SPD), keeps running into trouble. In addition, there are crises and wars. The German economy is facing more headwinds than seldom before, Merz said in October at the German Employers' Day conference in Berlin.

According to recent reports, given the circumstances, small successes are even more meaningful. "A heartfelt thanks for the good news you bring," Merz said when he received the autumn report of the Council of Economic Experts in Berlin, which predicted economic growth of 1.3% for 2026 and 1% for 2027.

In a recent development, the economic experts have a German government mandate to independently analyze business activity and make recommendations for economic policy. Earlier this year, they were much more pessimistic.

In a recent development, "The German economy has recovered quicker than expected from the energy price shock sparked by the war in Iran," said Monika Schnitzer, chair of the expert advisory board, explaining the prognosis. "We see a significant economic recovery, driven by surprisingly strong exports and high government spending.".

The chancellor, who celebrated his 71st birthday on November 11, spoke of "encouraging signals" in his address. "The economy in Germany is slowly on the rise again. Considering the many crises in Germany, it was not totally expected that we would manage that.".

But these improved prospects do not change the long-term problems. An ageing society means the bills for pensions, health and caregiving are constantly rising.

It has been revealed that at the same time, the number of working-age people who finance these services is sinking. That puts increasing pressure on the public purse. According to Berlin's financial planning, social welfare costs, defense and interest on debt will account for 80% of the spending in the federal government's budget.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"We must realize that in the long term the expected revenues in the federal budget will not be enough to cover the planned expenses," Schnitzer warned. The growth rates are far below what is needed to secure the same level of prosperity as previous decades in the long term.

"To grow out of this budgetary predicament, we would need levels of economic growth which we haven't experienced in Germany for the past 50 years," she noted.

The government is currently in final deliberations over its 2027 budget; spending upwards of €555 billion ($615 billion) is planned. Because revenue won't be enough to cover it, the government is planning to take on more than €118 billion in new debt. Adding the debt-financed special funds for infrastructure and the military, the new borrowing adds up to almost €204 billion.

The economic experts have warned that if Germany continues with this path, the debt-to-GDP ratio could rise to 100% by 2040. This ratio indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output. At the end of 2025, it was 63.5%.

Germany is the only country of the world's leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) to still hold a AAA rating, the best possible credit rating in finance markets. It signals to investors the smallest possible default risk for German government bonds. "I want it to stay that way," Merz emphasized.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that however, taking on less debt will not be simple. "A reduction in debt-based financing presents policymakers with a consolidation task of historic proportions and will require tough decisions," mentioned Schnitzer. The belt-tightening must, however, be designed to enable growth. Some recommendations include reducing environmentally harmful tax benefits — like the energy tax breaks for diesel fuel.

In a recent development, the so-called "mothers' pension", a pension subsidy for older parents, should be revoked, mentioned the experts. Tax increases could become necessary in the medium term, for example with value-added tax.

"The burden should be shared fairly between generations and societal groups," Schnitzer mentioned.

According to the chancellor, the experts' message has been received. Solid state finances are an issue in Germany but also throughout the European Union. Merz said there needs to be a consolidation course, adding that politicians have a duty to the younger generation. Reforms are needed, especially when it comes to social security systems.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Economic researchers are setting their hopes on increasing companies' productivity. Put simply, productivity describes how much a tech giant can generate with its employees, machinery and resources in a set time.

According to recent reports, according to the Council of Economic Experts, there is enormous variation even within the same industries. In Germany, the top companies are up to five times as productive as the weakest enterprises.

In a recent development, if the less productive companies caught up, economic growth could increase significantly, it stated in the report. "New technologies and business models could drive peak productivity and allow new highly productive companies to develop.".

But innovations need capital. It's here that the Ifo Economic Research Institute sees considerable deficiencies.

Latest evaluations show that German universities produce significantly fewer successful business startups than their counterparts in the United Kingdom or United States. For example, for every 1,000 students, about 14 venture capital-backed founders emerge from the vicinity of Stanford University each year. In Cambridge, the European leader, it's 3.5. In Munich, by contrast, it's only 0.5.

There continues to be an abundance of inventors and tinkerers in Germany, especially in mechanical engineering. However, the message from the industry summit in Berlin was that for renewed success, labor costs must come down. Suggestions included longer working hours and more flexibility for employers around job protection.

The intention was not to cut employees' wages and salaries. However, a upcoming study by the German Economic Institute commissioned for the German Mechanical Engineering Industry Association indicated that extending the working week by an hour alone would increase real gross domestic product by 1.5% in the coming five years.

Pochettino was given a rude awakening in his first match in charge of Man United as they were thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, with the game turned on its head in the eighth minute when Leny Yoro was given a red card for bringing Alexander Isak down just outside the penalty area as he headed towards the goal.

That doesn't help the Red Devils from what happened on the weekend, but it does at least ensure that Pochettino can select Yoro in the next game if he wants to.

Having now conceded more goals than any other team in the top five European leagues, it's clear where one of United's biggest issues is, and it was a nightmare first Premier League start in almost a year for Matthijs de Ligt.

Their other transfer priority is a upcoming striker in January, with the likes of Folarin Balogun and Ivan Toney mentioned alongside the Red Devils, with Pochettino knowing the former from his time managing the United States national team.

It could be one forward in and at least one forward out too, with a potential exit for Marcus Rashford still possible despite his reintegration into the squad at the start of this season.

Jacobs explained on the latest episode of GMS' Market Madness podcast:.

Rashford as well I still think is available at the right price, even though Man United have pitched it as being a reintegration into the squad.

Given it was well-publicised that United were willing to sell the England international in the summer, it's no surprise that the club would still be ready to offload him and his big salary.

It was expected that the 29-year-old would go in the summer following his successful loan spell with Barcelona, but the LaLiga champions decided to sign Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United instead.

With no other attractive offers on the table, Michael Carrick decided to bring Rashford back into the fold, and he started four of United's opening five Premier League matches this term.

The forward was then benched in one of Carrick's final games at Leeds United, before suffering a hip injury that has kept him on the sidelines since.

Rashford failed to make much of an impact in the final third during his eight appearances, and United will want to see more from him if he is to come back into contention in the coming weeks.

It will be interesting to see what Pochettino does with the Englishman, given one source close to the Argentine manager is mentioned to have claimed that he has 'always loved' the attacker.

It's quite well known that the 54-year-old tried to sign Rashford when he was in charge of Tottenham, and he clearly believes he is a player that suits his style of player and who he can get the best out of.

United chiefs could overrule him if the price is right, according to Jacobs, and it will be interesting to see if better offers arrive for the 29-year-old in the winter window.

  • "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he remarked on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three days after tearing up as he revealed his departure from the U.S. men's national team, outgoing head coach Mauricio Pochettino noted he does not want to think about the emotions that will hit him once the job comes to an end with Tuesday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti. He preached that it's still business as usual, even as one unusual week comes to a close and another equally unusual week begins.

According to recent reports, after two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity. The task in front of them on Tuesday is a simple one, especially after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti in the first leg – play like Pochettino's version of the U.S. team one last time.

"For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he remarked on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England. "I don't want to be disappointed. I don't want to lose the focus. I don't want to be less concentrated … [If] you take the game in a way that claims it's not vital tomorrow because it's already done, I think you will pay in the future – that lack of respect to the competition, to the opponent, to the result, to yourself. That is why tomorrow what I want is I'm going to put the best team possible and to perform.".

In a recent development, pochettino has been hesitant to reflect on his legacy after two years with the USMNT but that has been a common refrain during his tenure, spending just as much time molding the team's mentality in his image as he has their style of play. He leaves behind a mixed track record – results were all over the place in the build-up to the World Cup but it all appeared to come together once the tournament started, only for the U.S. team to fall flat on their faces in a round of 16 exit forever tinged by the Folarin Balogun affair. The stakes are undoubtedly lower against Haiti, the first leg advantage so substantial that the USMNT can probably survive another unimpressive performance before closing the book on the Pochettino years. There's a hint of succession planning in his looks for Tuesday, though, even if those plans are no longer his to execute.

"What I hope is to create the same link with us, with the new coaches that arrive here," Pochettino stated. "It's to create the same link with the players. [It's] become an emotional relationship, that you can find the best for this group of players that have enormous talent … That is an official game and it's the opportunity to keep growing for the future, to settle all the principles and grow and grow and grow.".

For all his faults and shortcomings, Pochettino does leave the national team in better shape than he found it. Some of it is out of his control – up and comers like Julian Hall, who scored on Saturday and now has four goals in his first five games for the senior team, were very likely poised for success no matter who the USMNT head coach was. After much trial and tribulation, though, he implemented a clear style of play and a cultural shift that several players have championed over the last week. Tuesday's game is ultimately a showcase for the players who will remain long after Pochettino leaves, both on an individual level as they aim to impress whoever takes the helm and as they try to prove a collective point now that the Pochettino years are over. U.S. Soccer's financial might may help sway Pochettino's eventual successor to take the job, no matter who that might be, but there is a pure soccer argument to taking this job.

Sources indicate that for perhaps the first time in its modern history, the USMNT can prioritize style of play with their next hire. That's true outside the reported approach for ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, whose interest in the job is unclear. Pochettino's high-intensity, attack-minded version of the U.S. team suited the players at this year's World Cup and feels especially tailor-made for the rising talents headlined by Cavan Sullivan, the 17-year-old Philadelphia Union attacker who is now MLS' youngest-ever MVP nominee. A strong outing on Tuesday will allow the Pochettino years to look like a stepping stone to an important newly introduced chapter, one that will hopefully get the best out of the experienced players as well as their younger teammates, no matter who oversees the project.

As for Pochettino, laying the groundwork for the USMNT's future comes while he focuses on his own. Assistant coach Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and sports scientist Sebastiano Pochettino departed for Manchester after Saturday's win over Haiti at Miami's Nu Stadium, filling in the gaps before Pochettino departs Cincinnati on Wednesday to begin his upcoming role. The rest of his coaching staff will stay in Ohio to finish out the international break with the USMNT before traveling alongside Pochettino.

Two years removed from starting a upcoming job with a short runway, Pochettino will do so again at United. The earliest he can oversee his first training session with United is Thursday, three days before an all-important clash with Liverpool. The longtime London resident, who previously coached Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, insists he will not be out of the loop when he finally makes his Premier League return.

"For me, it's not difficult," he stated of the quick turnaround. "I think we are well prepared to switch quick to like a player, from the national team to the clubs, from one game that you don't play well to another that you need to be ready again, from one action to the next action. I think we are well-prepared and then all the experience from the past, I think, helps us to be focused in the priority of the moment that demands that business. Today is to be focusing here in Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow but for sure, in the moment that game [finishes], we are going to start to be 100% focused in our next project … We watch soccer every day, all the leagues and we are always because that is our passion, our passion. We know the team [very well]. We know every single team [very well] and I think we don't need to match the preparation about the opponent. The most important [thing] is to know the details about our players, our staff, our culture, our identity and from there, to improve but now we are focusing [on] that game and we want to finish well tomorrow.".

A large task awaits Pochettino at United, who are right now in the relegation zone with just one win from their opening 10 league games of the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that jakob is 15 years old and attends a secondary school for more academic students, known in Germany as a gymnasium. He and his classmates have already been using artificial intelligence-enabled tools, or AI, for the last two and a half years.

Industry observers note that "I had a French test today, and yesterday I had ChatGPT explain a lot of the topics to me again," the student told DW. Jakob isn't his real name, because he doesn't want to publicly admit he and many others of his age use AI to do their homework.

Math, German, English, chemistry and even physics: In one click, the solution or the path to a solution is available thanks to AI.

In science, this is called "cognitive outsourcing." Basically, the required thinking is shifted to another device, whether that's a calculator, notepad or a large language model (LLM) like ChatGPT.

There's a difference with AI, though. A notepad or calculator can take over a step or two but rarely the whole thought process. That's not the same for an LLM, which can handle the entire problem-solving process.

Jakob admitted he's also had an AI help him with his homework. "But only when I was really stuck," he insisted. And he's also aware that it can become a problem when AI does all your homework. "The students who get good grades tend not to do that," he explained.

Franziska Müller has been a German teacher for several decades and is at the moment teaching senior classes at a gymnasium. Her name has also been changed for privacy reasons.

"They can't even think for themselves anymore," she told DW, complaining about some of her classes.

Industry observers note that even in ordinary classes, some of the students type their questions into their tablets or phones, asking for AI assistance. And should they be called upon in class, she knows that they're reading out the answers that the AI has prepared for them and hoping nobody notices.

Müller believes students these days are less able to comprehend text. "Because they read less and let AI summarize almost everything for them," she stated.

Several studies have reached very similar conclusions.

In a recent development, that includes the latest PISA (Program for International Student Assessment) study from September. PISA, which is run by the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, regularly evaluates the abilities of 15-year-old students around the world.

"Students who report using AI chatbots get lower scores in science, on average, than those who don't use AI," Andreas Schleicher, the OECD director for education and skills, wrote in his report in October. "This includes using AI to summarize texts they had to read, conduct preliminary research on a new topic, or draft texts for writing assignments.".

With participants from more than 90 countries, PISA is considered the largest international comparative study of 15-year-olds worldwide. This year, German 15-year-olds posted their lowest PISA scores in the 25-year history of the study.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"The connections are complex and depend heavily on how generative AI is used, but the central insight is simple: Just as we don't get fit by watching sports but by doing sports ourselves, learning doesn't come from consuming content, but from the mind's productive cognitive engagement with fresh material," Schleicher explained.

Put simply, those who don't exercise their brains risk becoming less intelligent.

US think tank, the Brookings Institution, has already argued that the risks of using AI in education outweigh the benefits.

Its own research, which included young participants from around the world, speaks of students losing "fundamental cognitive and durable skills as they increasingly rely on AI to perform learning's intellectual work," as well as the decline of critical thinking, memory, perseverance and independent judgment.

But what can be done against the power of ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini and Meta AI?

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has banned the use of AI in public schools up to the eighth grade for the 2026 and 2027 school years — so that's up to about the age of 14 or 15.

Industry observers note that not everyone agrees this is the right thing to do. Julian Hinn, who teaches German to students aged between 15 and 18 in Germany, remarked class members can still use AI apps on their mobile phones. "And anyone who thinks they won't use it at home is ignoring reality," Hinn told DW.

Germany's annual JIM study, which tracks teenagers' media use and device ownership, supports that view.

91% of young people surveyed in Germany, between the ages of 12 and 19, stated that they use at least one AI application. The study also reports that 74% use AI for homework and learning.

The last JIM study actually dates back to 2024 so those percentages might be even higher now. Data on AI use in Asia, Latin America and the US from the Brookings study show similarly high figures.

According to recent reports, german politicians have recognized the problem. Although education in Germany is the responsibility of the individual federal states, the so-called Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Cultural Affairs, or KMK, has been issuing statements on the use of AI since 2024.

The KMK's statements have been rather vague though, saying only that students should be enabled to engage with AI in a critical, reflective and responsible manner.

Teachers and students alike are aware that AI can be a powerful support in the classroom.

"The AIs simply explain things much better than textbooks," remarked Jakob, adding that he'll often get an AI to explain basic concepts to him.

Industry observers note that sometimes teachers can't respond like an AI, Hinn conceded. "The AI ​​can respond much better to the language and needs of the students.".

That's why he thinks it's notable to include AI in classes, starting from the 10th grade when students are around 15 or 16. Hinn doesn't think it should be introduced before that, when children's basic skills are still being developed.

Recent findings suggest that in more senior classes, Hinn will encourage his students to question the AI critically. "We look at the quality of the solutions," he explained.

German teacher Müller has also integrated some use of AI into her lessons for older students. But in some aspects of the class, she also bans it altogether so that her students can focus on thinking for themselves.

"I understand very well that it's tempting to use AI," she said.

Recent findings suggest that there are also other problems with AI in education. According to the Brookings study, students with basic skills can use AI to deepen their learning and progress faster.

It has been revealed that but for children with gaps in their knowledge, they tend to adopt AI's errors, outsource their thinking and then fall even further behind. In this way, AI can exacerbate preexisting inequalities.

The PISA study notes that children from more affluent backgrounds often have a better start, and AI can widen that gap.

This is called the Matthew effect — the name comes from the biblical verse Matthew 25:29, "for unto everyone that hath shall be given." It basically means that early success in learning leads to better progress in the future, while early struggles equal a growing lag over time.

In the age of AI, teachers have become more motivated to challenge students to think independently and to consider their own personal autonomy.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Hinn, who also supervises the school newspaper, said: "I always tell everyone, you can use AI but the feeling of having written an article with your own pen is spectacular.".

Recent findings suggest that both teachers also stress the idea of personal autonomy and responsibility. They believe this affects the students, especially because when they sit exams, they aren't allowed to use any aids or AI. And if they aren't able to solve their own problems, they will fail.

It's during exam time that the students really find out if they can solve those math, English or science problems by themselves.

It has been revealed that müller said one of her students recently confessed they were upset after a poor exam result. "He felt he simply couldn't think for himself anymore because of AI," she said.

This article was originally written in German.

The Luis Milla curler into the far top corner proved enough for Como to see off AEK Athens and surge towards the Champions League Round of 16, despite Lucas Da Cunha’s missed penalty.

The Lariani had won three of their first four Champions League games, despite missing Moise Kean and Assane Diao, with Maxence Caqueret not at 100 per cent either, but Trevoh Chalobah returned five weeks after his muscular injury.

AEK Athens lost their last three in Europe, but were leading Real Madrid twice until capitulating 3-2 in stoppages. Aboubakary Koita was sent off for dissent and therefore suspended, with midfielder Kervin Arriaga injured, but ex-Lazio goalkeeper Thomas Strakosha made his Champions League debut for this season after a wrist sprain.

See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog.

Lazaros Rota made a decisive defensive block to stop Tasos Douvikas meeting the Nico Paz through ball at full stretch, then Stavros Pilios got back to block Nico Paz on the counter, but the Argentine was booked for flailing an elbow into the defender’s face.

There were a few technical problems with the referee’s communication system, both before kick-off and during the first half, but he didn’t need help from VAR when Lovro Majer was very late to trip Alex Valle in the box.

However, Lucas Da Cunha slipped a little in the run-up and fired the penalty off target for Como. It was the first time in his career that the France international had failed to convert from the spot.

Jacobo Ramon couldn’t keep his header down from eight yards, and Alex Valle wasted a promising move with his scuffed finish past the near post.

Robert Sanchez needed a huge double save on the stroke of half-time, first on the Mijat Gacinovic deflected effort, then the Rota rebound too.

AEK had a huge chance after the restart, but Milan Vitalis couldn’t keep the finish down under pressure from a promising position after doing such good work to get into that situation.

Luis Milla with an unbelievable strike to give Como the lead 🥵.

Como survived the scares and took the lead when Luis Milla bent a right-foot curler into the far top corner from outside the area, on the Martin Baturina lay-off.

Jacobo Ramon’s header was just wide on a free kick, with the same for the Moukoudi attempt on a free kick from ex-Cagliari midfielder Razvan Marin.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, historically, goalkeeper has been a position of strength for the United States men's national team, to the extent that during the time of Tim Howard and Brad Guzan, both were playing Premier League soccer, but only one could start between the sticks. Things have changed since then, with numerous keepers coming through the ranks over the years, with most playing domestically or sitting on the bench for stronger European sides. However, that could be coming to an end for the team.

Industry observers note that during Mauricio Pochettino's tenure, Matt Freese has been his starting keeper, taking over during the Gold Cup and starting every game that he was available for until the September/October international window, when Pochettino used Diego Kochen and Brian Schwake. Kochen, who is playing his first season of first-team soccer at Lyngby in Denmark (where center back Neil Pierre also got his first taste of senior soccer), got the clean sheet against Mexico during that camp and turned that into a start against Haiti in Concacaf Nations League play in his native Miami, setting the USMNT up well to advance to the semifinals of the tournament.

Following that match, Kochen acknowledged that the USMNT squad has done a lot to put him in this position, and he'll know that even if Pochettino won't be the manager choosing the lineups, performances like this one will be vital for how the USMNT keeper picture looks moving forward.

It has been revealed that "I feel like I've grown quite a lot," Kochen noted following the match, reflecting on his adjustment to the national team. "I'm getting used to competing at the international level, but I've just got to give it to my team because they've been unbelievable. They make it so easy to just come out here and play free and be me, so without them, this wouldn't be possible.".

In a recent development, his growth is evident; one of the first things that comes to mind when watching the 20-year-old is his poise. Kochen had the ball at his feet plenty, completing all 20 of his passes to help send the attack on its way, and also made the two saves that he needed to on a mostly quiet night. His age also indicated when Haiti scored with him out of position, a goal that was called back for offside, but you take the good with the bad for young players because that's a learning moment, and as he earns more reps at the senior level, those are the kind of mistakes that can be ironed out.

"I'm not saying he hasn't played games in Barcelona, but at the senior level, every game he plays, he gets better and better and better," one of Kochen's coaches, Andreas Bjelland, told CBS Sports. "Because understanding the full-pitch play, and not only being on the line, just taking shots, and being a training goalie, but now he's playing for points every week. He's growing as a player, as a person, and as somebody we can trust more and more in the stuff we do. So it's nice to see that it has come to this ... It's quite impressive.".

You can't teach poise, and spending more than five years in the Barcelona system shows in how Kochen carries himself. It's becoming more common in American soccer for young players to test themselves abroad or to get into Major League Soccer teams at a younger age, and when they succeed, it goes a long way developmentally, as Kochen's case shows.

"He is a person who trusts himself a lot. That's also why he's a good goalie, that at such a young age he hasn't that big of a doubt of himself," Mikkel Jespersen, Lyngby's other coach remarked. "He knows what he's capable of doing, and that's really important as a goalie: that you trust yourself and know what things you are doing is something that can succeed in a longer period.".

Industry observers note that while it's unknown what the next USMNT manager will value in a keeper, being able to perform in an uncertain environment with your coach having one foot out the door is something that will go a long way for Kochen's chances. In keeper terms, Kochen has plenty of time ahead of him, as players at his position regularly play until their late 30s or early 40s, so if he can continue this trajectory, the question of who protects the net could be solved for the foreseeable future.

It has been revealed that of course, that's a lot of projecting, but when the next generation of the USMNT is developing at an astounding rate, it's only natural to think about where players like Kochen could end up. Doing this in only his first season of professional soccer is already impressive, but the best is yet to come.

While there can be little doubt about Unai Emery’s status as an elite manager in the modern game, matches at the Nou Camp continue to be the stuff of nightmares.

His record at Barcelona now reads 15 defeats from 16 matches and this was another difficult evening with Aston Villa unable to banish the demons for the man who has transformed their club.

According to recent reports, it was Emery’s 55th birthday and with the Prince of Wales and Prince George both in attendance, Villa fans were hopeful of another memorable European night. But from the moment midfielder João Gomes handed Barcelona their opening goal, it was always going to be an uphill struggle.

Emery has suffered many uncomfortable occasions at this grand old stadium, none more so than the notorious “La Remontada” of 2017 when he last competed here in the Champions League with Paris St-Germain.

It has been revealed that this latest visit would become his heaviest defeat in Europe as Villa manager. With three wins from the opening four matches, they still have a fine chance of progressing to the knockout stage. Yet, aside from the mistakes, there will be a sense that Villa could have capitalised more against a team in the midst of a defensive injury crisis. They did have a number of chances in the first half but were left to rue their lack of ruthlessness.

Recent findings suggest that at the heart of Barcelona’s victory was Lamine Yamal, their outstanding jewel from the academy. The 19-year-old became the highest-scoring teenager in Champions League history, eclipsing the record of 13 he previously shared with Kylian Mbappé, with the opening goal.

Yamal was orchestrating everything from the pace of the match to the volume of the supporters, at one point imploring them to raise the noise in the first half with both arms aloft.

There was also another impressive performance from England international Anthony Gordon and Raphinha, who dedicated his two goals to the memory of Jesus de Miguel, the Tenerife forward, who died on Tuesday.

With that tragedy fresh in the minds and the Nou Camp under construction, it was a peculiar atmosphere at times.

The defeat marked the end of Villa’s 100 per cent record in the competition, with a tough test away at Galatasaray up next before they host PSG in December. They remain high up in the table and have often displayed a propensity to bounce back promptly from defeats.

In a recent development, emery mentioned: “We are in a process and this was a very good test against a team like Barcelona. We are not at the level we want to achieve but there are a lot of experiences for us to take. Overall, we are competing fantastically in the Champions League and there is still work to do.

“Over the process we’ve had here, we have made mistakes but then overcame them. We accept this defeat but take a lot of information from it.”.

Nine years have passed since Emery’s last visit in this competition and time has not proved a great healer.

Then in charge of PSG, Emery witnessed his team surrender a 4-0 first-leg lead to lose 6-5 on aggregate. Any matches where he is involved at the Nou Camp will revive memories of that remarkable comeback. He must have feared a repeat of more pain when Yamal, making his 37th Champions League appearance, rewarded Barcelona’s early pressure.

Villa’s defending needed to be as close to perfect as possible, but they were exposed after a poor error of judgment from Gomes. Under pressure from Barcelona’s attackers, Gomes panicked and played a blind pass into the path of Yamal, who bent his left-footed shot into the corner.

That mistake could have threatened to damage confidence but Villa did respond. Matty Cash’s half-volley from inside the penalty area was only a few inches wide, while Johan Manzambi side-footed wide of the goal after a quick break down the right from Nicolas Jackson.

It has been revealed that with Andreas Christensen, Eric García, Xavi Espart and Jules Koundé all absent here, Barcelona’s defence did appear vulnerable. Jackson was targeting the flanks and having his more dangerous moments challenging their high line. Emery paced his technical area, imploring his players to remain focused.

It has been revealed that yet Barcelona’s forward three were always a threat and they increased their lead eight minutes into the second half. Raphinha was given too much room to turn in the penalty area and his shot took a heavy deflection off the heel of Pau Torres to find the bottom corner. Emery was furious, appearing to raise his fist in the air at another poor goal conceded.

Barcelona added a third goal with Raphinha converting from close range after a sublime pass from João Cancelo.

Raphinha dedicated his goals to De Miguel, who died on Tuesday after sustaining serious injuries during a match the previous night. He mentioned: “Tonight I don’t want to talk about football. I want to send a lot of strength to Jesus de Miguel’s family.

Industry observers note that “May he rest in peace. In the end, this can happen to anyone. The truth is that it’s very tough. When we saw the news this morning, it was complicated. I’m incredibly shocked and sad. In the end, you go to play a match, and the same thing could happen to you. From myself, from the club, we want to send a lot of strength to his family.”.

Villa did continue to fight for a consolation, with substitute Leon Goretzka heading against the post and their 3,000 travelling fans continued to sing in the rain after the final whistle.

This was the first encounter between the two clubs since the European Super Cup Final in January 1983, and yet another reminder of the upward trajectory under Emery.

Unai Emery has managed more than 1,100 matches but will never forget the drama of “La Remontada” as he returns to the scene on Tuesday night.

Emery is back at the Nou Camp in the Champions League for the first time since one of the most epic games in the history of the competition. While in charge of Paris St-Germain nine years ago, Emery took his team to Barcelona with a 4-0 lead from the round-of-16 first leg. Yet he was left stunned as Barcelona recovered to win the rematch 6-1, with three goals in the final seven minutes and the winner proving hugely controversial.

Sergi Roberto’s goal five minutes into added time caused a massive backlash as PSG claimed it was offside, with Emery claiming on Monday that the match revealed that VAR was “necessary”.

Industry observers note that aston Villa have made the trip over to Spain to take on Barcelona in the Champions League on matchday four. These teams last met all the way back in 1983, when they met in the European Super Cup. Barcelona won the first leg 1-0 at home before Aston Villa claimed a 3-0 victory at Villa Park, meaning Villa progressed 3-1 on aggregate.

Aston Villa have made the perfect start to their Champions League campaign, winning all three games, beating Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking, scoring 12 goals in the process. Unai Emery’s side drew 1-1 at home against Fulham in the league on Saturday. Emery, who celebrates his 55th birthday today, has a very dismal record against Barcelona, taking just three wins from 30 matches. His last Champions League game at the Nou Camp was infamous as his PSG side lost 6-1 to go out in the last 16 back in 2017 despite winning the first leg of that tie 4-0.

Sources indicate that “In 1982, Villa won the European Cup, and we like to think about playing in this competition again and trying to repeat that success,” Emery stated. “Barcelona are favourites for what they have done in the last ten years; now they need to prove why they are favourites.

It has been revealed that “[Barcelona] have [Lamine] Yamal. He is a special player. You can see in him as a player who could end up being the best. He needs a few things but he could end up being a great player. Rodri gives personality to the team. They have [Anthony] Gordon giving them speed and hard work. They have Pedri or Fermin [Lopez] as offensive midfielders.”.

Barcelona started strongly in the Champions League, winning their first two games, but lost 4-2 at defending champions PSG last time out. They warmed up for this match with an emphatic 6-1 win over Alaves in La Liga on Saturday. That victory gives them a two-point lead at the summit of La Liga.

Sources indicate that “We know that at this level, anything can happen,” Barcelona boss Hansi Flick said. “Against Real Madrid, the result could have been different. These are special matches, but we are staying confident. It is normal to focus more on our last two defeats, but I have confidence in my team, which showed it again on Saturday. Now, we are focused on the Champions League, with the goal of finishing in the top eight. For me, he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world and he has reaped extraordinary successes. His team’s style of play is clear and very well organised. Just look at how they execute set pieces; it is something impressive. Their confidence in themselves is unmatched. It will be a tough match against a great team and a great coach.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There is no more room for error in the 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League.
  • OL Lyonnes rule the league phase at the moment.
  • The final six clubs with the least amount of points will see their Champions League dream end, so matchday 5 will be a crucial turning point for several teams.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is no more room for error in the 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League. After four matchdays, the league phase has been whittled down to only two games left for each of the 18 clubs, and the margin between a bye into the quarterfinals and an extra round of knockout playoffs in February will come down to dwindling points.

OL Lyonnes rule the league phase at the moment. They top the tournament table with ten points, level with FC Barcelona but with a superior goal difference. Just behind the two Champions League contenders are Bayern Munich and Arsenal, with Chelsea FC and Manchester City creeping closer to the top four. Out of the 18 clubs competing, only four will earn direct berths to the quarterfinals, and eight will compete for a future spot alongside them.

The final six clubs with the least amount of points will see their Champions League dream end, so matchday 5 will be a crucial turning point for several teams.

Fighting for top spot positioning will be Arsenal and OL Lyonnes, and Chelsea against Paris Saint-Germain. HB Koge, Roma, and tournament debutants Inter Milan are level on four points and need to be in full urgency mode if they're to leapfrog and remain in contention for future rounds.

Here's what to watch on Matchday 5:.

Manchester United's shockingly bad season has seen yet another player express interest in leaving the club in January.

The Red Devils sit 19th in the Premier League after just one win from their opening 11 games, having been thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield in Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge since replacing Michael Carrick in the dugout during the international break.

The result also means that United have conceded 34 goals in all competitions this season, more than any other team in Europe's top five leagues, and the club are now understood to be eyeing potential signings for the January transfer window in order to bolster the squad.

Central defenders Harry Maguire, Matthijs De Ligt, Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven and Lisandro Martinez are all competing for minutes, while Diogo Dalot, Noussair Mazraoui, Patrick Dorgu, and Luke Shaw are the full-back options.

But after a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid earlier this season, Argentine defender Martinez expressed his anger at the club's hierarchy and their squad building in the summer, and a 2027 exit is now seen as almost inevitable, with his contract due to expire in June.

However, it has now emerged that he is not the only Man Utd player open to an exit in the January window, with Ayden Heaven now looking at his options.

According to BBC Sport, the 20-year-old defender is considering an exit away from Old Trafford in January as he feels he will not be afforded the opportunities to play regularly and develop with Man Utd's current situation.

Heaven is now on his third permanent manager since joining the club in January 2025, but was an unused substitute for Pochettino in the Liverpool game and feels that could become a more common theme, with the team battling against a surprise relegation.

The former Arsenal man understands that Pochettino could look to more experienced options, and reports that the club are looking to sign a upcoming centre-back will see him drop further down the pecking order too. A loan or a permanent move will be considered, with his current contract running until 2029 with the option of a further 12 months.

Reports have been swirling since the summer that Man Utd are planning a defensive rebuild for 2027, with Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw also out of contract alongside Martinez.

There have also been question marks around the futures of Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs De Ligt following their performances this season, and it's clear that there are several upgrades needed across the back line.

Recent findings suggest that fulham star Calvin Bassey and Brentford's Nathan Collins have been linked for January, while Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite is a long-term target, but none of those deals will be easy to do mid-season. However, if a deal can be done, then it would make sense to allow Heaven to move on temporarily until the summer, and then review his position at the end of the season.

He's clearly very talented, and being left-footed means he can add some balance to the side too. But he knows he isn't the obvious solution to their problem right now, and his development would be best-served with him playing elsewhere rather than sitting on the bench.

Six Maths Essentials: How to Model the World Terence Tao Pelican.

Recent findings suggest that can knowing about central principles in mathematics help us to understand our world? Leading mathematician Terence Tao — who has been called the Mozart of maths — explains how it can in his latest book, Six Maths Essentials.

Sources indicate that can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world.

Recent findings suggest that can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world.

For Tao, the six concepts are the building blocks of reality that together provide an opportunity to better understand it. They are, he writes: “numbers as the gateway to quantitative thinking, algebra as the gateway to abstraction, geometry as a way to go beyond what we can see, probability as a tool to navigate uncertainty with rigorous thinking, analysis as a means to tame the very large or very small, and dynamics as the mathematics of change”.

In a recent development, each is described with elegant minimalism, consistent with Tao’s vocation of writing concise mathematical proofs. In its brevity, the book evokes physicist Richard Feynman’s Six Easy Pieces (1994), which explains fundamental physics concepts to the layperson. Similarly, the beauty of Tao’s book is seeing maths through his eyes, describing its spirit as well as generalizing across the discipline.

Recent findings suggest that for instance, Tao describes how artificial intelligence inspires awe and magic — it easily lives up to science-fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke’s famous statement that “any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic”. But AI has a dark side, too. It can lead us to become superstitious and think that the tool cares about us, or to develop a sense of fear that we wouldn’t know how to live if it malfunctioned.

Tao makes the case that maths has played an important part in the story of humanity. We meet famous mathematicians such as ninth-century Islamic astronomer Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī, who pioneered algebra, following in the footsteps of the ancient Babylonians, and gave his name to the Latin form of the term algorithm. Others solved real-world problems, from calculating the distance between Earth and the Sun to understanding the 2008 global financial crisis.

We learn about mathematicians who overcame the desire of philosophers such as Immanuel Kant to pigeonhole geometry into a single ‘true’ concept, instead finding that there is a plurality of connected geometries. Other mathematicians revealed the laws of chance through their passion for gambling.

AI has transformed maths — this is how we got here.

AI has transformed maths — this is how we got here.

Tao invokes hardly any equations, opting instead for intuitive explanations. It is through this same intuition, Tao argues, that children work out that there is no highest number, thus deducing the concept of infinity. He discusses the elegance of algebra and its ability to solve many problems without requiring a tailored equation for each application. This generalizability, he notes, is what distinguishes maths from organic chemistry — which was his least favourite subject in school, he writes, because it required memorizing disparate facts without organizing principles like those found in maths.

According to recent reports, he is at his best explaining difficult topics to the public. On analysis, he writes that there are both hard and soft aspects, corresponding to quantitative and qualitative modes. He calls analysis the accountant of maths: “auditing and proving which techniques work under what circumstances”.

Industry observers note that he uses mathematician John Conway’s Game of Life to demonstrate the need to study dynamics. In this game, simple rules are applied to a matrix of elements that are either ‘on’ or ‘off’ as they unfold into complex patterns. The grid functions as a rudimentary yet, in principle, fully functional computer.

John Conway used games to transform mathematics.Credit: Dith Pran/NYT/Redux/eyevine.

Importantly, Tao conveys how mathematicians think as they discover fresh maths. He distinguishes the ‘cold’ maths found in textbooks from the active maths that happens as mathematicians explore fresh domains. For example, he describes how Carl Friedrich Gauss imagined what it would be like to be on the surface of a sphere — a view that led to his “remarkable theorem” on the properties of curvature, proved in 1827.

It has been revealed that we should start with the video. It’s something to behold. Opening with a scene that depicts a young footballer being ushered through a crowd of faux reporters, there is a promise within the first five seconds of ‘epic news’ and ‘a rare discovery’.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a little on-the-nose, but the messaging will only escalate. Soon we find ourselves staring at what appears to be a Ballon d’Or replica, before the director cuts to a moody shot of the footballer from behind as he stares at a wall of photographs.

Those images are showing a few of the staging posts in his brief career to date – signing for Manchester United aged 10, posing with a ball and, then, one of him preparing to come on as a substitute. A pair of Nike boots find their way in.

Finally, the lad highlights himself and delivers a single line to camera: ‘I am epic.’.

It has been revealed that this came out at the start of the week. Our epic footballer? That would be JJ Gabriel, aged 16 years and one month, still in braces, and potentially the best you’ve not yet seen.

As you have likely heard, he really is that good. And as you will also know, the mechanisms of his exit from United ahead of an imminent deal with Real Madrid have been ugly.

JJ Gabriel, aged 16 years and one month, still in braces, and potentially the best footballer you’ve not yet seen.

The video Gabriel released this week announcing his exit from Manchester United includes signing for the club at the age of 10 alongside Cristiano Ronaldo Jr (Source: Instagram/Jjnr10).

Finally, the lad shows himself and delivers a single line to camera: ‘I am epic’ (Source: Instagram/Jjnr10).

But let’s momentarily keep to that bizarre video, which has been watched almost two million times on Gabriel’s Instagram page, and from there we can raise the question of whoever thought it was a good idea.

In a recent development, this is where we should introduce Ali Barat, the owner of Epic Sports. He’s a substantial fish in the world of football agencies and the 31-second clip was advertising their latest coup: Gabriel had joined his group, which is timely because a move to Real is imminent and that will follow other big deals brokered by Barat.

They include Moises Caicedo to Chelsea for £115million, Noni Madueke to Arsenal for £52m and Dean Huijsen to Bournemouth for £12.6m, then on to Real Madrid for £50m more. He’s a significant figure with a changeable definition of what it means to be understated. Here’s an example from his firm’s website: ‘While some agents seek the spotlight, Ali Barat is quietly reshaping the transfer market.’.

Amusingly, it then goes on to describe Barat as a ‘super-agent’ twice in the same paragraph while declaring he is ‘not just closing deals, he is building careers, guiding legacies, and setting the standard for a fresh era of football representation’.

In a recent development, the ‘quiet’ part was possibly lost along the way. But ‘legacy’ is the word among that salad most worthy of fixation, because Gabriel has been steered to a series of pivotal decisions at an incredibly young age.

He is yet to play a single minute of competitive senior football but he is clear on what he wishes to become. Earlier this month, his handlers felt it prudent to place him in an interview with the Madrid-based newspaper Marca and Gabriel remarked: ‘My dream is to win a Ballon d'Or.’.

It has been revealed that fair enough. He’s a teenager aiming high. Is it wise to say so? Maybe not, but he’s 16. Barat, the super-agent, has no such excuse. He’s 30 years older than his client and saw no harm in a video that invoked the Ballon d’Or to peddle an academy kid.

There’s less ambiguity in the wisdom of what Barat has done there. It reeks. It carries the stench of an agent who evidently doesn’t mind so much if the labels attached to Gabriel today stick for the remainder of his career.

Earlier this month, his handlers felt it prudent to place him in an interview with the Madrid-based newspaper Marca and Gabriel remarked: ‘My dream is to win a Ballon d'Or’.

Gabriel's representative Ali Barat, who is 30 years older than his client and saw no harm in a video that invoked the Ballon d’Or to peddle an academy kid.

I can remember when Mauricio Pochettino once made the blunder of placing Marcus Edwards, a Tottenham wonderkid, into the same sentence as Lionel Messi. His point was that he had some similar movement patterns, but the fact the lad was named mini-Messi in training didn’t help – it was a tag that endured.

Thankfully, Edwards has carved out a respectable career at Burnley via Sporting in Portugal, but Pochettino regretted the words as soon as they left his mouth.

That’s different to designing and releasing a video, of course. That’s different to a process involving some level of sign-off. That’s different to the grubby act of hyping a very young guy to a standard reached by only five Englishmen in history.

A question at this stage: where was Gabriel’s family when this was being decided? That’s somewhat loaded because there is chatter about how much of the United separation has been driven by Gabriel’s father, Joe O'Cearuill, formerly a professional himself for Brighton, Barnet and the Republic of Ireland.

I’d add that many of those noises have originated from within Carrington. It might simply be the bitter discourse of the jilted. But a recurring sentiment among some United staffers is that the father became difficult during the breakdown in relations.

In a recent development, these are lines we have heard before in football. But for once, United do not appear to have done much wrong. There was genuine care for the player. And if there is one thing they can guarantee, it is that young talents get a good chance, though evidently not enough to please Gabriel’s camp.

A demand for minutes against Azerbaijani side Sabah in the Champions League was a bad look; similar might be said with less force around reports that he changed his name from Joseph Junior Andreou O'Cearuill for commercial reasons, feeding one of those blurry conversations about where the athlete ends and the product begins.

Gabriel’s early days with Epic and Barat and his content wing do not serve much encouragement on that front.

Gabriel's father Joe O'Cearuill was briefly in Arsenal's reserves before going on to play for Brighton, Barnet and the Republic of Ireland.

United do not appear to have done much wrong. There was genuine care for the player. And if there is one thing they can guarantee, it is that young talents get a good chance.

It is worth stating that the teenager at the heart of it all is not considered to be a bad sort. Far from it.

None of his ascent was accompanied by the worrying noises that followed another prodigy in Ravel Morrison – once described by Sir Alex Ferguson as having 'as much natural talent as any youngster we ever signed', but who made all of three League Cup appearances for United before a journeyman career through the Championship, Italy, Mexico, Sweden, the Netherlands, the US and the UAE.

One source has suggested Gabriel even cried when he stated his goodbyes back in September.

It might be over-reaching to claim he has left the club against his own better judgment, but there is no doubt he has gambled hugely on Real Madrid.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is pretty handy and has found it tough there; Martin Odegaard is a far closer parallel to Gabriel having moved to Madrid aged 15, and he played 11 games in three seasons.

If the pathway was blocked at United, then what is it at a club who employ Vinicius Junior, Rodrygo, Yan Diomande, Arda Guler, Endrick, Brahim Diaz, Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe in Gabriel's positions?

A latest language and surroundings are large hurdles for a young player, especially one whose ambitions are so public and grand. It won’t be a quiet arrival by any definition, even those found in the quirky dictionary of Ali Barat, and the pressure will be significant.

Hopefully such factors don’t impact upon an exciting trajectory. That would be an epic shame.

It has been revealed that among the joys of this job is being present at rare moments of sporting greatness. The Welsh win over the All Blacks last weekend was one such occasion and, for me, it was compounded by a subsequent email from a lovely chap named John Evans, aged 87 and from Tredegar in Blaenau Gwent.

John had watched the game on television, but was part of what must be a dwindling group who could say they were there the last time Wales had beaten Newly introduced Zealand, at the Arms Park in 1953.

Recent findings suggest that after detailing how he, ‘a small-bottomed outside-half’, had left himself with no view of the pitch at the back of the stand, John went on to recall that the crowd around him and a friend ‘decided to pass us over everyone’s head back down to the front’. He landed just in time to see Ken Jones score the winning try. His excitement in sharing a memory from 73 years ago was spelled out in block capitals.

Recent findings suggest that one of the consequences of the ongoing shambles at the Welsh Rugby Union is that there were 20,000 empty seats at the Principality Stadium last weekend, mainly due to a combination of apathy and protest. Accordingly, there will be 20,000 fewer people with a great story to tell decades from now. While the WRU ponder their next blunders, they might wish to consider some of the above.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a farewell for Mauricio Pochettino before he heads to Manchester United, the United States men's national team were able to defeat Haiti 2-0 on Tuesday night, advancing in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals 8-0 on aggregate. Christian Pulisic opened the scoring with a bicycle-kick goal to kick things off, which was the emphatic send-off that was needed prior to Pochettino arriving in Manchester, but the USMNT were able to keep things up in the celebration in Cincinnati.

CHRISTIAN PULISIC GET ON YOUR BIKE‼️#USMNT x @VW pic.twitter.com/Yb3yqXfC33.

In a recent development, julian Hall followed with a poacher's goal as Weston McKennie played orchestrator, and it continued a theme that whoever ends up taking over the national team will have tough decisions ahead. Folarin Balogun is struggling for minutes with Monaco and is looking to make a move at the end of the season, and Hall has done everything that he can to increase his own standing with five goals in six games for the USMNT.

Sources indicate that the New York Red Bulls star has a ways to go considering that he's still only 18 and will need to gain experience against top teams in the world instead of just Haiti, but he also can't ask for a better start than what he has gotten off to. It's why this is such an attractive job for whoever takes over the USMNT. They'll be able to build upon the good that Pochettino has instilled; the talent is there to move the squad forward, and there's plenty to love about the youth of the USMNT.

And alongside that, Pulisic has essentially screamed don't forget about me. During this camp, the Milan man has followed up on signing a new contract with the club by reaching 35 national team goals, moving into fourth all time for the USMNT over Eric Wynalda. Diego Kochen added to the good vibes with a third straight clean sheet, and Neil Pierre was even able to be cap-tied against the nation that he's also eligible for as the full-circle moments were left and right.

Pulisic, the former 17-year-old phenom, was subbed off for Cavan Sullivan, the current 17-year-old phenom, and while the goal difference may have been larger in the first leg between these sides, this felt like a more measured performance despite the strangeness of Pochettino's assistants heading to United while he managed the squad prior to catching his own charter.

It has been revealed that this camp had every chance of being a disaster given the circumstances of Pochettino leaving, but all parties did what was needed during this camp. All dual nationals were capped, including Santiago Castaneda, showing that even on his way out, Pochettino made sure to take care of the future of the federation. On to the next round of the Concacaf Nations League with a upcoming manager and no complaints with the performance so far for the squad.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Max Allegri admits Napoli did something ‘really well for the first time’ in the 2-2 draw with Manchester City to keep Champions League ambition alive, and assures Kevin De Bruyne ‘will remain until June.’.
  • The Partenopei came to the Etihad fearing the worst amid an injury crisis that left them without 11 players between fitness, suspension and the Champions League list.
