📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Max Allegri admits Napoli did something ‘really well for the first time’ in the 2-2 draw with Manchester City to keep Champions League ambition alive, and assures Kevin De Bruyne ‘will remain until June.’.

The Partenopei came to the Etihad fearing the worst amid an injury crisis that left them without 11 players between fitness, suspension and the Champions League list.

Instead, they leave here with regrets after twice taking the lead through Rasmus Hojlund and Noa Lang, only to be clawed back by Ayyoub Bouaddi and the Rayan Cherki angled drive.

A 2-2 draw is still a positive result, especially away to Enzo Maresca’s side, and keeps them in the hunt for a play-off spot.

“This match was important, because if we win at least one of the last three, we should be in a good position for qualification,” Allegri told Sky Sport Italia.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a very difficult game, the lads did well, and obviously there were moments when we had to suffer under pressure, but for the first time we really did well out of possession to slow Manchester City down. They did really well in that.

Sources indicate that “It was a deserved draw, ultimately we leave here with a bitter taste in our mouths, but I told the lads that the belief, the courage is necessary in Europe, as there are spaces to play in. After this, we must prepare in the best way for Sassuolo, tonight was a good training session above all for our defence.”.

Considering the circumstances, it is remarkable to see Napoli leaving Manchester City feeling regret, as they were decimated with barely any options to come off the bench.

“We should be happy with the point, which is the most notable thing, but also the performance. There were moments when we should’ve made more of their high line, and had a couple of good situations, but we were against a very strong opponent. The lads applied themselves brilliantly.”.

Allegri was asked if this was his most satisfying evening yet on the Napoli bench, especially as there haven’t been many high points yet in his tenure since taking over from Antonio Conte.

“I am above all happy for the lads. When you play in the Champions League, you need that extra belief, to even be arrogant, and trust your abilities.”.

This was an emotional return to Manchester for Kevin De Bruyne, who was given a hero’s welcome by his former fans, and a standing ovation when substituted late on.

“Unfortunately, age waits for no man, but he is an extraordinary player. It made me sad to take him off today, as he rarely makes a mistake with the ball at his feet. Players like De Bruyne and Luka Modric, for those who love football and admire the sport, they represent something special.”.

De Bruyne will be out of contract in June 2027, but there are multiple reports he could leave for PSV Eindhoven in January.

“We’ll discuss it with the club, but he is a very professional lad, and I think he will remain until June,” assured Allegri.

Napoli have been leaking goals all season, and Allegri took responsibility for their struggles.

According to recent reports, “I think in the first part of the season, above all for my responsibility, we didn’t do enough to prepare defensively. We conceded too many really silly goals, for example against Bodo/Glimt when conceding for 4-3 straight after going 4-2 up.

It has been revealed that “That is a bad sign, it is a sign of a lack of respect and humility from the team in certain moments of the match. We made Manchester City sweat to score goals today, they had to do something extraordinary, and that is how it should be, with this determination in the tackle and total concentration in every game,” concluded the coach.

Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1050 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal.
  • But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.
  • As a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal. More than 80 countries backed the idea.

But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.

As a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap. At the same time, a group of 57 countries frustrated with the deadlock at the consensus-based UN talks decided to form a "coalition of the willing" to accelerate the fossil fuel exit outside the COP framework.

They held their own summit in April in Santa Marta, Colombia — the first such conference to specifically focus on implementing the transition away from fossil fuels (referred to as TAFF).

Co-hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands, the Santa Marta conference brought together countries including Canada, Norway, Brazil, Nigeria, Mexico, Australia and Germany, as well as highly climate-vulnerable states such as Vanuatu.

The idea was for governments to start developing national roadmaps and working out how to restructure their financial and trade systems to wean themselves off polluting energy sources — an incredibly complicated undertaking, particularly for developing countries dependent on revenue from fossil fuel exports.

Part of their discussions focused on cutting subsidies for oil, coal and gas, as well as supporting people whose livelihoods rely on the fossil fuel industry to find new forms of income.

A little over six months on from the Santa Marta meeting, representatives from almost 200 countries are holding talks in Antalya, Turkey, as part of the latest UN climate conference.

Countries agreed for the first time in 2023 to transition away from fossil fuels — the main driver behind rising global temperatures. But summits since then have failed to pin down how to implement that pledge.

It's not yet clear whether the Santa Marta coalition will influence ambition at this year's COP.

"I think it's more of a long-term game," noted Chetna Hareesh Kumar, a climate policy analyst at the Berlin-based research organization NewClimate Institute.

Industry observers note that she says it's too soon to expect the coalition to have an influence on the negotiations but adds that that could change at future COPs. The grouping could bring more nations on board if, for example, it reveals it can be truly inclusive, address the needs of different types of countries and show that a transition is feasible.

One role the group is playing, according to Alexandra Scott, a senior climate diplomacy adviser at Italian climate change think tank ECCO, is "keeping up the political momentum," and showing "that there is this huge group of countries who really want to accelerate this transition away from fossil fuels.".

She claims it's also building an invaluable "cadre of knowledge" on how to develop national TAFF plans and deal with barriers individual countries face — like how to secure funding for the infrastructure investments needed for the energy transition.

The Santa Marta group is "really answering a lot of the questions that countries have always had on how on earth do we even start to transition our whole economy off fossil fuels?" Scott remarked.

This expertise being shared and tested in practice can show what such a transformation could look like and the knowledge brought into COP, added Scott.

Sources indicate that since the Santa Marta conference, Germany, France and the Netherlands have released national looks to phase out fossil fuels. While the plans contain no fresh commitments, experts see them as a positive first step.

Industry observers note that kumar says more countries could announce similar prepares just ahead of the second TAFF summit in Tuvalu next year. Finland presented its TAFF roadmap in the first week of COP, but analysts do not expect many more countries to follow suit soon.

Another potential boost that could get momentum going is Brazil's recently published global roadmap to transition away from fossil fuels, promised at last year's COP.

The nearly 200-page document seeks to serve as a toolkit for countries shifting from fossil fuels to renewable energy, such as wind and solar. It envisages countries making a phased transition between 2028 and 2033.

The aim, Ana Toni, CEO of last year's COP, told AP, is to break down the transition into "smaller actionable solutions" and help countries make practical progress.

In a recent development, the roadmap suggests measures tailored to each country's circumstances, including dependence on fossil fuel and financial capacities. "Levers" it proposes include reducing fossil fuel subsidies, expanding renewable energy and cutting methane emissions.

Kumar called it a "customizable" approach that allows every country to take action, regardless of its situation. "The question really is now what countries do with it and how much momentum they can generate," she added.

This year's climate change summit in Turkey — taking place after a series of deadly heat waves in Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that killed more than 1,400 people — isn't expected to result in any big announcements about fossil fuels.

Global renewable energy capacity has surged in recent years, making up a third of the world's power generation for the first time in 2025. But many countries still rely on coal, oil and gas.

A database compiled by the German environmental organization Urgewald shows that most oil and gas companies worldwide, among them QatarEnergy, Saudi Aramco and Russia's Gazprom, are exploring or developing new reserves.

Meanwhile, subsidies for fossil fuels amount to around $920 billion (around €830 billion) per year, according to data from the OECD, but that number is falling.

One problem Turkey is pushing at the COP conference is electrification. It's calling on countries to endorse the goal of 35% of final energy consumption coming from electricity by 2035 — up from around 20% today.

The pledge has drawn criticism from some circles, though, for leaving open whether that additional electricity needs to come from clean sources.

Ideally, Kumar said, electrification would be powered by renewables and tied to a goal of phasing out polluting fossil fuels.

"If something like that could make it to the final text, that would be a really good sign for momentum.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rob is senior football editor at GiveMeSport, with over 15 years experience covering sport in various capacities since graduating from the University of Gloucestershire in 2008 with a degree in journalism. A childhood obsession for all things football developed into a career writing about the beautiful game, initially producing content for clients including Luton Town Football Club and the PGMOL. His first big interviews were with Premier League referees Howard Webb and Michael Oliver in 2009. He then spent four years producing written content for a betting website, mainly focusing on football, and was there to cover various games and tournaments including the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012. Rob joined GiveMeSport in 2013 (initially as a sub-editor before becoming a senior writer and then senior editor in 2020) and has covered countless football matches and other sporting events, interviewed various high-profile figures including Rio Ferdinand, Peter Crouch and Theo Walcott, and written well over 10,000 articles during that time. Rob has played a key role in GiveMeSport's coverage of the World Cups in 2014, 2018 and 2022, plus Euro 2016, Euro 2020 and Euro 2024, along with many Champions League finals. While football is Rob's area of expertise, he has also covered a wide range of other sports during his time at GiveMeSport including boxing, tennis and darts, as well as the 2016, 2020 and 2024 Olympic Games.

Manchester City were left fuming on Tuesday night because they felt referee Istvan Kovacs blew the final whistle too early at the end of their Champions League clash against Napoli.

The two sides played out a 2-2 draw at the Etihad Stadium, but City were convinced Kovacs ended the game before the allotted two minutes of stoppage time had elapsed.

Enzo Maresca’s side were pushing for a winning goal after Rayan Cherki equalised in the 86th minute. However, those associated with the Premier League club were left incensed when the referee blew his whistle for full-time.

It has been revealed that the Athletic’s Manchester City correspondent Sam Lee wrote on X (Twitter): “The ref blows the final whistle and points to his watch to tell the angry City players that the game is over. The big screen clock showed it was 91:47, and two minutes had been added on. They're still arguing now.”.

Man City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, one of the best goalkeepers in the world right now, was shown a yellow card for his protestations as boos rang out around the Etihad Stadium.

City right now sit sixth in the Champions League table with 10 points, but could find themselves out of the top eight by the end of Wednesday night if results don’t go their way.

A win would have left City on 12 points, level with the likes of Paris Saint-Germain (who face AS Roma on Wednesday), Como and Real Betis.

An explanation has now emerged, explaining why the ref appeared to blow the full-time whistle early.

The TV broadcast shows the Romanian match official actually blew the final whistle at 92:04 - not 91:47, as the significant screen inside the Etihad Stadium claimed.

TNT Sports commentator Darren Fletcher said: "There's a problem here, the Manchester City bench are furious. I think they're saying he's blown before time, and so are the City players on the pitch.

"The clock on the screen was actually 20 seconds behind our clock, so if his watch tallies up with our clock he's got it right - just to make that point while all this pandemonium breaks out.".

While it remains unconfirmed at this stage, it seems likely that the problem was caused by the Etihad Stadium big screen’s clock being slightly behind.

Kovacs’ timing tallied with the TV broadcaster’s on-screen clock, which suggests the match was brought to an end at the correct moment.

The Predator Elite, instantly recognisable for its fold-over tongue, is reimagined in BAPEâs signature green ABC CAMO with gold stripes, a shark graphic on the lteral, alternating gold logos on the tongues, and ABC CAMO sockliners.

Meanwhile, the F50 Elite features a striking blue-to-pink gradient ABC CAMO upper, shark graphic on the medial, and clear star prints across the surface. Both pairs are showstoppers built to turn heads on and off the pitch.

Beyond the boots, the collaboration extends to footwear and apparel, including reimagined adidas Sambas with a BABY MILO skull face in rubber, ABC CAMO jerseys, shorts, tights, and a BABY MILO football tee.

Accessories complete the set, with an ABC CAMO duffle bag and a BABY MILO shoulder bag rounding out the collection.

Fronted by Real Madrid and Brazil legend Marcelo, known for his flair on and off the pitch, the 'adidas x BAPE' football collection is a truly global statement piece, appealing to fashion fans and football enthusiasts from Asia to the Americas and Europe.

The collection drops September 6th via Confirmed, adidas.com, select adidas retail partners, BAPE.com, and BAPE STORE locations worldwide.

  • When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the new head coach of Manchester United.
  • The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:25 EST, 22 November 2026.

When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the new head coach of Manchester United.

The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.

However, United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25 left Carrick’s job hanging by a thread. He was given a two-week stay of execution that also allowed United time to step up their search for a suitable replacement.

At a meeting of the club’s executive committee on November 5 – after United had lost to Chelsea and staged a chaotic Champions League win against Roma – it was decided that Pochettino would be the No.1 choice if Carrick was sacked.

By the time the Argentine caught that flight to Atlanta 24 hours later to take charge of the USA's two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, United were preparing to make their move.

This is the story of the whirlwind two weeks that will end with Pochettino taking charge of his first game as United boss against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday following the dramatic events on both sides of the Atlantic.

Patrick Dorgu’s injury-time header rescued United from another defeat as they snatched a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, but it wasn’t enough to save Carrick. His fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp.

There is a five-hour time difference between Manchester and Georgia, so it was late afternoon when Pochettino first learned of United’s interest at the Trilith Guesthouse – close to the US national team’s training base in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta – as the players began to report there for duty.

Michael Carrick's fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

As speculation raged over Carrick’s future, the odds on Pochettino replacing him at Old Trafford were slashed after some major money was placed on the 54-year-old overnight.

Industry observers note that preliminary talks continued with his representatives who made the US Soccer Federation aware of the situation. Pochettino discussed it over dinner at the team hotel with chief executive JT Batson and chief operating officer Dan Helfrich who knew it was pointless trying to change his mind.

Recent findings suggest that ‘That was the significant day,’ notes a source close to Pochettino, who took US team training in Fayetteville. ‘It became real and the optimism grew.’.

As talks accelerated between United and their prospective fresh head coach, Carrick returned to Carrington to work with the United players not on international duty while chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and rubber-stamp the change.

United reached verbal agreement with Pochettino over a two-and-a-half-year deal, and agreed to pay US Soccer around £10million to buy the 54-year-old and his staff – No 2 Jesus Perez, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino (Mauricio’s son), strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott – out of their contracts.

It has been revealed that there was never any question of him leaving before the two Haiti ties, even though it left little time before his first game against Liverpool. Pochettino is said to have been respectful of the USA’s position and felt an obligation to see the job through.

As a compromise, it was agreed that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr would be allowed to leave for Manchester after the first leg regardless of the result.

Sources indicate that media in the US were informed that access to the players had been cancelled out of respect for Veterans Day. It also meant that they don’t have to answer questions about Pochettino’s future.

Carrick returned to Carrington at 7.50am for the last time as United head coach and was sacked in a meeting with Berrada and Wilcox.

By the time Pochettino woke up in Fayetteville, United officially had a managerial vacancy and he gathered the players together for a scheduled team briefing at 10am.

Pochettino went through the usual pre-match preparation, and then invited staff into the room for the second half of the meeting.

There was some emotion but no surprise when he informed them of his decision to take the United job. ‘As you’d expect, he spoke from the heart,’ says a source. ‘He loved being here but United was a dream opportunity. It was too hard to say no, but hard to say goodbye.’.

United officially revealed Pochettino’s appointment and confirmed that he would stay in charge for the USA’s two games against Haiti before starting work the following Wednesday.

Pochettino conducted his pre-match press conference in Fayetteville, flanked by CEO chief JT Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, and broke down in tears as he thanked them for their support over the last 26 months.

Otherwise, the preparation is stated to have gone according to plan as the US squad flew to Miami.

The Argentine broke down in tears as he thanked the USA for their support over the last 26 months.

The US smashed Haiti 6-0 to all but guarantee their place in the semi-finals. Even so the message from Pochettino to his players after the game was: ‘This tie isn’t over.’.

The players learned for the first time that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr were leaving camp, and they headed straight to Manchester.

Pochettino flew with the players from Miami to Cincinnati for the second leg at the TQL Stadium.

On a visit to the Kenwood Towne Centre shopping mall, a man whose profile had risen in the US during his two years in charge of the national team was approached by even more fans than normal.

When Pochettino appeared as a guest of honour at the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium that night, a number of Bengals’ players and staff congratulated him on his fresh job claiming to be United fans.

It emerged that United had provided a private jet for Pochettino and the remainder of his staff to fly straight from Cincinnati to Manchester through the night after the second leg.

In his pre-match press conference, he confirmed the departure of his three coaches over the weekend, and it was no surprise to learn that he was in constant contact over several days as he prepared to join them at Carrington.

Sources indicate that the US beat Haiti by two goals to complete an 8-0 aggregate win. Afterwards, they played Take Me Home, Country Roads by John Denver over the stadium PA, which has been a tradition since the US hosted the World Cup last summer but carried particular poignance given that it has also been adopted as an anthem at United.

Pochettino invited all the staff onto the pitch for a team photo as he led a chant of U-S-A, and there was a tearful send-off in the dressing-room as he was presented with a signed shirt and a special hand-painted bottle of Clase Azul tequila.

It’s a favourite tipple of Pochettino’s and staff also ordered food from Chick-fil-A, which Pochettino regrets won’t be available in Manchester.

He never had a permanent residence in America, so he left the stadium at 10.30pm with the same suitcase he had brought from London and headed for Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport for the flight to Manchester.

Pochettino had a poor night’s sleep before landing shortly before noon aboard the grey Gulfstream G700 jet with D’Agostino, Scott and Tuya.

He posted a picture from the skies above Manchester and was then driven to Carrington, changing into an official United tracksuit en route.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino was too late for training but met with some of the players and club executives before being given a tour of the training ground and conducting an interview with MUTV which wrapped up about 7pm. He stayed at the training ground long into the evening to catch up on his preparation for Liverpool.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United.

More players returned from international duty, but Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online. It was proof – if he needed it – that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will be under even greater scrutiny at United.

Responding, Pochettino stated: 'We have young guys training with us. It’s not nice. It’s not good.

'What do they want to show? Yes, we were working on shape. We were very organised. What is the point of doing something that can be very dangerous?

'I don't want to be upset, but I think it's a process the club is caring a lot about.'.

Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online.

Having only trained for a couple of hours on Thursday, Pochettino worked with the players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

‘The training session was a little bit longer than it normally is in (match day) minus two,’ mentioned Pochettino at his opening pre-match press conference, admitting that he had not even had a chance to shower beforehand.

Pochettino worked with his new players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

Pochettino took training for the third day running at Carrington on Saturday morning, before United travelled on the team bus to their hotel where they had dinner and a pre-match meeting last night.

On Sunday he faces a massive first game as United boss in front of the cameras at Anfield at the end of a dizzying fortnight.

Andoni Iraola looked up to the ceiling of Fenerbahce’s media auditorium as he tried to find the words to describe the madness he had just witnessed.

According to recent reports, “Cheap” was his first conclusion, swiftly followed by “messy”; technically, Liverpool’s head coach was right but this was a moment when nobody would have found issue had he gone further. “Absurd” and “preposterous” would have been more accurate portrayals of this calamity.

Sources indicate that liverpool have won two European trophies in Istanbul, but they do not tend to enjoy visits to Turkey. Roy Hodgson, in August 2010, was the last Anfield manager to oversee a win here and there was an irony that the hero of that night in Trabzon – Dirk Kuyt – masterminded this downfall.

Kuyt, interim head coach, got a remarkable response out of a Fenerbahce team who had amassed 1,086 Premier League appearances between them and he was as giddy as the locals after Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and substitute Vedat Muriqi scored to give the club a famous night.

“It’s frustration because it’s a difficult place to come here and to play,” said Iraola. “During most of the game, we were thinking: ‘OK we can win this one.’ But obviously it hasn’t happened. We conceded, I think, messy goals, especially the first and the third one. The second one is a rebound.”.

Liverpool have made the long trip to Turkey to take on Fenerbahce on matchday four of the Champions League.

Sources indicate that liverpool enter this fixture having won all three Champions League matches thus far, beating Atletico Madrid, LASK and Villarreal to make it nine points from nine for Andoni Iraola’s side. Liverpool’s five-game unbeaten streak was ended by Arsenal in the league on Sunday. They return to the city where the club enjoyed one of their most memorable nights, beating AC Milan in the Champions League final 21 years ago.

“Istanbul is always going to be very special for Liverpool,” Iraola remarked. “It is difficult to find a more crucial night. Tomorrow [tonight] it won’t be easy, you talk about statistics, especially English teams playing here. They have very good players and a very good squad, they know how to play in this competition. We have to start strong in the game. It is very early in the season to establish comparisons. We want to continue how we have done in the Champions League, three games and nine points, it is a good chance to get to 12 points and then finish in the top eight. Champions League away is very difficult.”.

In addition to the long-term absentees Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Giovanni, both Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong have missed the trip to Turkey.

According to recent reports, fenerbahce have made a slow start to their Champions League campaign, taking just two points from their opening three fixtures. They have drawn twice against Roma and Slavia Prague at home whilst they suffered a heavy 6-0 loss at Aston Villa. Former Liverpool forward Dirk Kuyt has been appointed their interim coach following the resignation of Ismail Kartal following their recent defeat to arch rivals Galatasaray just over a week ago.

“It is a great opportunity for us to show what we can do,” Kuyt stated. “It is also a great opportunity for me, a game between two teams that are very notable to me. We have a very good plan, and we have to believe in this plan. No-one who loves Fenerbahce is happy with the current situation, but this is a huge opportunity. We have players who have won the Champions League and the World Cup.”.

They come into tonight’s match having lost back-to-back league games since drawing against Slavia Prague on matchday three of the Champions League. They have plenty of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Ederson, N’Golo Kante and Romelu Lukaku.

Germany dominated neighbor and historic rival the Netherlands in their Nations League quarterfinal match-up at Berlin's Olympic Stadium on Monday evening.

It was the team's sixth game under head coach Jürgen Klopp and the 50th ever between the two sides.

Germany's 5-0 shellacking of the Oranje was their most lopsided victory since 1959, when they won 7-0. In all, Germany have now won 19 of those matches, the Netherlands have won 12, and 18 ended in a draw.

Industry observers note that speaking to German broadcaster ARD after the game, attacking midfielder Florian Wirtz — who scored twice in the fixture — mentioned: "We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second half.".

Despite the loss, Xavi Hernandez's Dutch side will reach the final eight alongside Germany.

Prior to the match, Klopp had made it clear that he and his team were approaching Monday's showdown as a final after having lost to Greece 1-0 in his first home game in the job on September 27.

By night's end, Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck each scored once and Brajan Gruda scored once and added two assists on top of Wirtz's double.

Klopp has been high on Wirtz, who has come under fire for not delivering at Liverpool since his arrival there in June 2025, and his bet seems to be paying off with the 23-year-old now scoring four goals in his last four games for Germany.

"We don't care who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly," said Wirtz on Monday evening before adding: "We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we've taken some great steps in our development as a team.".

A group of five EU member states, including Germany, have entered talks over a scheme to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda.

The strategy to set up so-called return hubs in a non-EU country had been announced by the group — which also includes Austria, the Netherlands, Greece and Denmark — had first been announced back in September.

Tesla has earmarked some €3 billion ($3.3 billion) to expand its factory in Germany, near to Berlin.

The Grünheide complex will be expanded to start producing the electric car organization's driverless Cybercabs, with output expected to eventually reach 1 million units.

The Elon Musk-owned company said construction would begin in 2027, with the first Cybercabs rolling off the line in 2029.

"With this, we are laying the foundations for the world's most technologically advanced Tesla factory here in Grünheide," Tesla remarked.

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.

Matt Pearson on our sports desk breaks down where the power struggle currently stands, with the deadline for candiates just a matter of hours away now.

Lawmakers in the state parliament in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania have voted in Manuela Schwesig for another term as state premier.

The 52-year-old has been in the role since 2017 and is heading into a third term.

The vote was a secret ballot, but it can still be assumed who voted and how.

She received 39 of the 68 votes cast in the chamber, exactly as many as commanded by Schwesig's three-party coaliton of her Social Democrats (29), the ecologist Greens (5), and the socialist Left Party (5).

While Söder's comments in Munich focused in particular on the policy the coalition in Berlin had not delivered, Merz initiatlly focused on talking up the efficacy of his federal coalition.

"We are aware of the situation. We know that we now need to deliver. And we also know that we face difficult talks within the coalition. But I would also say from the experiences of the last weeks that there are solutions to the problems which we have in Germany," Merz said.

Merz said that in the 18 months since last year's election, the coalition "has already successfully implemented many things, not 'set them into motion' as people like to say, but actually implemented.".

He noted a total of 17 bills going through the second and third reading process in the lower house of parliament, the Bundestag, last week, "including the most comprehensive reforms of our intelligence and security services that we have ever done in [post-war] Germany.".

Among others, he thanked Bavarian Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, a senior member of the Bavarian CSU sister party to Merz's own conservative CDU, for his contribution to this.

Merz also touted the support given to CSU politician Ilse Aigner, not just from his CDU but from the Social Democrat coalition partners and the Greens, to become the next president, calling her a person who would "represent our country very well at home and abroad.".

After hailing these accomplishments, Merz then turned to electricity tax cuts, saying he anticipated talks on the matter on Tuesday that would be "very short.".

He said that over the weekend, coalition leaders had revisited the figures, and now believed they would be able to "completely" reduce electricity taxes to the minimum European levels in 2027 "also for private households.".

Bavarian state premier Markus Söder has appeared with Friedrich Merz at a press conference during the chancellor's trip to Munich.

It seems Söder, Merz and the CDU/CSU believe they have unfinished business after the budget was finalized in the Bundestag late last week.

Merz had pledged in the run-up to the decision to provide a reduction in electricity tax for all, but the final agreement did not include this step, with the coalition partners the Social Democrats (SPD) saying it was not adequately costed.

Söder stated he and Merz had discussed "backup for the coming days," for Berlin and for a "collective stance, that is really, really important.".

He mentioned the coming days were about "demonstrating credibility in politics," seemingly in reference to Merz's promise that the coalition did not ultimately deliver.

According to recent reports, "That's why it's really key to us that we do indeed bring about the reduction in electricity tax," Söder said. "This is important for businesses. It would be a relief for citizens. But it's also a matter of credibility and it's written in the coalition agreement.".

Söder said that as to the question of "where the money comes from, with a €560 billion (roughly $615 billion) budget, with €200 billion in new debt, nobody can tell me there's no potential within the budgeting process.".

A festive piece of merchandise on the right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) "fan shop" website has upset some religious leaders in Germany.

Called a "chocolate Nicholas," it appears to depict a semblance of Saint Nicholas in bishop's regalia and the party's colors and holding a book with "AfD" written on the cover where a Bible might be in more traditional iconography.

The Bishop of Essen, Franz-Josef Overbeck, was highly critical of the promotion in Monday's edition of the Bild newspaper.

Sources indicate that "The AfD is appropriating Christian symbols for party campaigning," Overbeck mentioned. "Showing the holy Nicholas in a blue coat with mitre, staff and the gospel with an AfD logo is not in order.".

Overbeck acknowledged that other organizations like football clubs would sell chocolate Christmas figurines in club colors, but he said they would tend to refrain from including overtly Christian symbols when doing so.

Bild quoted an AfD spokesman as saying that as a "liberal-conservative party that clearly associates itself with Christian values," the item fit "particularly well" with the party image.

The main German protestant church group EKD's cultural representative, Johann Hinrich Claussen, stated the offer revealed the AfD had "no understanding of traditions and no respect" for Christianity.

He described the action as "embarrassing and revealing," and said that Christianity was "supra-partisan.".

Sources indicate that "The AfD knows little about what is holy to Christians. Otherwise, it would be aware that Bishop Nicholas of Myra, in what today is Demre in Turkey, stood clearly for uniting the occident and the orient. Beyond that, he is the patron saint of rescues at sea," Claussen mentioned.

The partner of deceased Bavarian politician Hubert Aiwanger has said that anybody is welcome at his funeral this coming Saturday.

Aiwanger was the economy minister in Bavaria's state government as the leader of the junior coalition partners to the center-right CSU.

"Hubert was a man of the people and so it stands to reason that anyone who liked or treaasured him is allowed to come to his funeral," Tanja Schweiger wrote on her Instagram profile overnight.

Recent findings suggest that she was posting after a requiem in the state capital Munich paying tribute to the leader of the Free Voters (Freie Wähler) party over the weekend. Around 1,100 people attended this ceremony.

Aiwanger died suddenly and unexpectedly on November 4 during a working visit to Berlin, aged 55.

Prosecutors have since mentioned he died of natural causes, after he was found dead in his hotel room.

Germany's national men's football team will play neighbors and rivals the Netherlands for the 50th time on Monday night.

And there's quite a lot at stake for Jürgen Klopp's team in the last group stage game of the Nations League competition at Berlin's Olympiastadion.

If Germany win, they will qualify for the knockout stages, but a defeat could lead to potential relegation into the second tier of Nations League football.

Klopp was upbeat in the pre-match press conference at the prospect of playing the Netherlands, who he stated play "Xavi football," in the image of the skillful Spanish playmaker and World Cup winner coaching the team.

"I've always loved playing against teams like this. For all my coaching career," Klopp said. "When someone notes, 'hey they can really play football,' then in my mind the party's already started.".

A full house with some 71,000 fans is expected in the capital when the game kicks off. Klopp played on the Dutch reputation for liberal use of bicylces in his comments to reporters, saying he wanted to "put a stick in their spokes" and dislodge them from the saddle.

According to recent reports, the notion of a bridge over the valley between Ratingen and Heiligenhaus to the east of Düsseldorf in western Germany as part of the A44 highway is more than half a century old. And the physical bridge itself has stood, complete, ever since 2022.

Yet still the crossing is not connected to any roads at either end.

A construction project to build the last 4.4 kilometers of highway and link the bridge to the A44 highway will formally start on Monday.

State premier Hendrik Wüst, as well as the regional transport and traffic ministers will attend the ground-breaking ceremony.

A project first conceived some 55 years ago has faced repeated delays because of lawsuits, environmental protection studies and onerous planning and permit procedures.

The bridge across the Angerbachtal (Angerbach Valley) should improve the road connection between the North Rhine-Westphalia state capital of Düsseldorf, the Bergisches Land mountain range and the industrial cities in the Ruhr Valley. It's also meant to help remove some strain from the perenially busy A3 highway and to improve the road connections to Düsseldorf International Airport.

The last stretch of highway is expected to cost around €200 million (roughly $220 million), or roughly the annual costs incurred each year by forcing traffic to divert around it, according to estimates from Düsseldorf's IHK industry and trade association.

Construction is expected to take several years, no formal end date has yet been set.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz heads to Munich early on Monday, for a meeting with the leadership of the Bavarian Christian Social Democrats (CSU), the sister party to his conservative  Christian Democrats(CDU).

No concrete details about the talks were made public ahead of time, except for the CSU saying it would serve as a general exchange that had been planned for some time.

The trip comes a week after Merz nominated Ilse Aigner as the next German president, likely paving the way for her to become the first woman and first CSU politician to assume the role.

It also follows soon after the 2027 federal budget cleared a marathon meeting of the parliamentary budget committee in Berlin. This serves as one of the more conspicuous examples of the frictions and difficulties in the grand coalition between the Christian Democrats and the center-left Social Democrats — with the compromises it contains a point of frustration among the CSU and for state premier Markus Söder.

The northeastern state parliament in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania will likely vote in Social Democrat (SPD) Manuela Schwesig for another term as state premier early in the afternoon.

The 52-year-old, who first stepped into the role in 2017, intends to lead a new coalition of the SPD, the environmentalist Greens and the socialist Left Party after state elections in September.

The right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) emerged as the largest single party in the sparsely populated state.

But still, the political calculus that emerged was arguably simpler than in Berlin — where the socialist Left Party is the largest party but could struggle to lead a coaltion — and in Saxony-Anhalt, where the AfD was by far the largest party but short of an outright majority.

Schwesig's SPD claimed 29 seats, with the Greens and the Left each taking 5, meaning that when combined, they hold a fairly clear majority over the AfD with its 32 seats.

Sources indicate that the SPD's relatively successful performance in the state, at least compared to its national struggles, has also led to Schwesig being linked with a possible return to federal politics. The SPD looks to elect a newly introduced leadership duo early next year.

Schwesig has already had a spell in Berlin as the federal minsiter for families, pensioners and women, and briefly led the SPD on an interim basis in 2017, but after this she returned to her home state to seek the top regional job instead.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz is starting his week in Munich, at a meeting of the Bavarian CSU sister party to his conservative Christian Democrats (CDU).

Recent findings suggest that in just nine short days, eight teams will compete in a quarterfinal round. The USWNT will face El Salvador on Nov. 27 in the quarterfinal round, and if they advance, they'll clinch a spot in next year's World Cup. The other matchups are Canada against Panama, Mexico vs. Haiti, and Jamaica will play Costa Rica.

"It's been a great year of growth and learning for our team, and for a long time the focus has been on qualifying for the World Cup, so now that time has arrived," said Hayes.

Sources indicate that "I want to see relentless consistency from our players, individually and as a team, and I want us to be elite in both penalty boxes. If we can achieve that, I'm confident those performances will carry us through to meet our standards and goals. This is my first Concacaf event and the first for many of our players, so we're all looking forward to the experience.".

Sources indicate that hayes selected a full roster that features several players competing in their first-ever senior-level World Cup qualifying tournament, and a handful of veterans. Just eight of the 23 players selected were members of the 2022 Concacaf W Championship roster: forwards Mallory Swanson, Trinity Rodman, Sophia Wilson, and Ashley Sanchez; defender Emily Fox; and midfielders Lindsey Heaps, Rose Lavelle, and Sam Coffey -- who joined mid-tournament that year.

Sources indicate that coffey returns to the roster after missing two previous international windows while managing a lower-leg injury. Defender Naomi Girma is out as she continues to manage a lingering calf injury. The centerback has not featured with the national team since April, and has yet to play with Chelsea FC this season. Midfielder Olivia Moultrie is currently rehabbing from an ACL injury sustained in August. Other notable omissions on the roster are Jaedyn Shaw and Ally Sentnor, both of whom have been part of U23 and senior camps throughout the year.

This is just the third camp for the attacking line of "triple espresso" since the 2024 Olympics. If the trio starts a match during the Concacaf W Championship, it will be the first time they start a game together since the gold medal match. Both Swanson and Wilson have worked their way back into senior camps over the year following maternity leave.

Sources indicate that ashley Sanchez's return to the roster comes after standout performances against Spain last window and a stellar 2026 NWSL regular season where she won the Golden Boot with 20 goals scored. She was also nominated for the 2026 NWSL MVP award. A positional shift to left winger and an outrageous amount of scoring have all led her back to the USWNT due to consistent performances, a key factor for Hayes with her large player pool.

It has been revealed that "Be consistent first of all in performance. Ashley Sanchez wasn't on our radar, not because she isn't talented, but there were certain things we demanded from the performance that I think she has delivered in her game on a regular basis. So, I think that's the first thing. I think you've seen that includes Croix Bethune coming into this camp -- been outstanding in the number 10 position all year, and would have been in last camp as well if she was fit. You do have to consistently find consistent performances, particularly if you're a player that doesn't have credit in the bank," Hayes mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that as the World Cup gets nearer, finalizing a roster for the 2027 summer tournament is even closer. Things like consistent form and senior-level experience will come into play when naming a final 23 for the World Cup for Hayes.

"If you're a Mallory Swanson and delivered on a world stage on a regular basis for the national team, it does alter things slightly. No, we don't want players that are in our group that are in a place where they're not fighting to improve every day or be as competitive as they could possibly be, but I think when players have stacked and accumulated a lot of experience over a period of time, that is always going to put them in a steady position," Hayes explained.

"But it doesn't guarantee anything. I will be unafraid to leave anybody off that plane if I don't feel that they are applying themselves to put ourselves in the best possible position to compete. Which is why this upcoming camp, our job is to qualify for the World Cup, and so everything we have worked towards is ensuring that every player that comes in at camp makes sure they lift their level and they position the team to have the most positive outcome, regardless of the opponent. And I'd be demanding as much as I always do, but I have a big expectation from our senior players to step up.".

Recent findings suggest that el Salvador is the eighth-ranked team in the Concacaf W Championship and earned its spot following a preliminary qualifying round. The group is coached by manager Eric Acuña, who recently made headlines for harshly criticizing his players in a press conference following losses to Paraguay last month.

Still, Hayes and the staff aren't taking any opponent lightly no matter the rankings or state of the locker room.

"It's a team that knows is competing for something, so it doesn't matter the opponent; they're competing to go to a World Cup, and do I think that will be it will be demanding and taxing? And yes, I do. In many different ways, because the expectations are all on us. I think for them, it's how are they going to disrupt us and make it difficult? But they have two players in the front line that can cause a lot of problems, particularly in transition. So we have to set up for that," Hayes noted.

"I think when it when it comes to the players, I've always championed creating positive environments for players. And yeah, I'm sad for the players to hear what they've gone through, but as always, I can't control that. I want the best for players all of the time in their environments, but I am here to represent the U.S. and try and help us qualify for the World Cup. So my focus is on that. Even if my heart goes out to the players and I think we still have a lot of work to do in the women's game to keep driving female-centered, female-lens environments where women can thrive.".

Klopp wants Infantino out as FIFA candidate deadline looms

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (864 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has become the latest prominent football figure to call for change at the top of FIFA.
  • "Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job," he remarked on Sunday.
  • But with time running out before the November 18 deadline for upcoming candidates for the presidency of world football's governing body, Infantino is looking overwhelmingly likely to win another term.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has become the latest prominent football figure to call for change at the top of FIFA.

"Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job," he remarked on Sunday.

But with time running out before the November 18 deadline for upcoming candidates for the presidency of world football's governing body, Infantino is looking overwhelmingly likely to win another term.

"There are people who truly care about the future of football, people who aren't driven by financial interests," Klopp stated ahead of Germany's Nations League match against the Netherlands on Monday.

"If someone like that were to step up — if someone like that were to become president — I think that would be a significant improvement.".

If that person is waiting in the wings, they're leaving it late to step on the stage. Despite a raft of federations and continental confederations, including Germany, UEFA (Europe), CONCACAF (North and Central America and the Caribbean) and AFC (Asia), calling for Infantino's head in the wake of his plan to sell off part of the World Cup earlier this year, the incumbent appears to have stopped the bleeding.

That proposal, which involved forming a subsidiary arm of FIFA called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) in order to sell off part of its commercial operations to investors including Joshua Kushner — brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner — was widely panned before being abandoned.

It followed on from widespread criticism of Infantino's awarding of a fresh FIFA Peace Prize to Trump, the overturning of a red card for US national team player Folarin Balogun, and with Trump's involvement, at the World Cup and a host of other controversies.

Since then, though, many public critics have backtracked amid FIFA promising to release an extra $2.7bn (€2.45bn) from its reserves over the next four years to the federations, increasing their total investment to $6.35bn.

Perhaps the most significant of these u-turns came from the AFC, who went from saying Infantino had committed a "fundamental breach of trust" in August, to offering the Swiss its "full commitment to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a latest mandate as the FIFA president" in October.

Those words were spoken by AFC President, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, who ran against Infantino when he first won the top job at FIFA in 2016. He will not run again and remarked that "my feeling is, I'm sure, the feeling of most of my members," in regard to Infantino.

Sources indicate that proof that the sentiment is not universal comes in the shape of Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japan Football Association (JFA). Tashima is one of only two people to confirm they will oppose Infantino in the March 2027 presidential elections.

It has been revealed that the 68-year-old is a well respected figure in Asian football politics and will have no problem meeting the threshold of support from five of FIFA's 211 federations. This is not like the other candidate, former Swiss international player Ramon Vega, who is an enormous outsider. Tashima appears to be running on the basis that he will be able to chart a calmer path at FIFA.

Recent findings suggest that "I am grateful that I can make this announcement with the full support of the Japan Football Association," Tashima told the Japanese newspaper Sports Nippon. "It's not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built. What FIFA needs now are these values that we have protected. I have decided to run in order to make this appeal to the world.".

But the numbers are against him. Though support from within the confederations may not be total, the backing of AFC and the African confederation (CAF) is a huge boost for Infantino, with those two alone making up 101 votes, almost enough for a majority.

In fact, the only real concern remaining for Infantino remains UEFA. The European federation, headed by Aleksander Ceferin, is a major revenue source for FIFA but the two organizations are at loggerheads. As well as a war of words, UEFA are seeking to obtain evidence for a potential Swiss criminal case against Infantino in regards to FFE. FIFA have called this a "smear campaign" and a "fishing expedition".

According to recent reports, but, so far, UEFA has not put up a candidate. Former Arsenal coach turned FIFA Chief of Global Football Development, Arsene Wenger was thought to be a contender but has now ruled himself out. Wenger's compatriot, Philippe Diallo, has since emerged as another option, with The Guardian reporting on Monday that the French Football Federation president could be announced on Tuesday.

It has been revealed that while Europe is football's powerbase, particularly from a club perspective, UEFA will need Diallo, or any candidate they can convince to run, to win votes from outside its 55 nations to have any chance of success, particularly with Tashima likely to split any challenge. Even if a candidate appears before the November 18 deadline, Klopp's hope for change appears to be a long shot.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WASHINGTON, D.C. – By the time U.S. Soccer confirmed Mauricio Pochettino's departure for Manchester United early Friday morning, the announcement itself was far from a surprise. The press release included the usual formalities – Steve Cherundolo, the U-23 U.S. men's national team head coach, would fill in for the Dec. 13 friendly against Jamaica that falls outside the FIFA international match calendar, and the assurance that the search for Pochettino's USMNT successor would begin shortly. Federation CEO J.T. Batson and COO Dan Helfrich will unsurprisingly lead the search, as will "the soccer leadership team at U.S. Soccer that includes" assistant sporting director Oguchi Onyewu. There was one unique detail tucked into the announcement, though.

Emma Hayes, the U.S. women's national team head coach, will also have a say in the matter.

Sources indicate that men's and women's national teams rarely overlap at any given federation, largely because there's little need for a crossover event. They operate on different calendars and in the best case scenarios, each team has dedicated members of staff. Hayes' name-drop as news of Pochettino's exit became official, then, is a unicorn-like sighting, even if U.S. Soccer often champions a spirit of collaboration between all of its national teams. It is uncommon for the head coach of one senior national team to help recruit a counterpart but in U.S. Soccer's case, it makes complete sense.

Industry observers note that hayes' coaching career, which spans two decades and two continents, means her inclusion on the federation's soccer leadership team is an obvious one. She is amongst the most respected soccer minds in the game, which easily makes her one of the most vital people on U.S. Soccer's payroll no matter how you look at it. That will be especially true in a hiring process that has to conclude with a compelling follow-up act to Pochettino's splashy arrival two years ago. Her perspective might actually be vital in the process, which only adds to the intrigue of what's next for the USMNT.

According to recent reports, "We have an extraordinary gift, which is a women's national team manager who's incredibly insightful, bright mind about the sport, who has a set of personal experiences and relationships that span the club and international game, the men's and women's game, the domestic and international club game, and who also has lived in the shoes of what it's like to be a U.S. national team senior coach," Helfrich told CBS Sports on Thursday. "It is a no-brainer that that mind and that voice has a really prominent seat at the table when we're talking about key moves for the federation.".

USMNT coaches are rarely style hires; look no further than the list of people to hold the job on a full-time basis this century and the picture paints itself. The only thing Bruce Arena, Bob Bradley, Jurgen Klinsmann, Gregg Berhalter and Pochettino seem to have in common, outside of the job they all once held, is that they were all tasked with some sort of cultural reset depending on the task at hand. That likely will not be the case for Pochettino's successor, though, who will inherit a team with a clear style of play, a healthy mix of veteran players and rising talents and plenty of time on the clock until the next World Cup. The job will be defined in part by continuity, even with the necessary allowance for the newly introduced hire to put their unique spin on things.

Industry observers note that that's where Hayes' expertise should play a crucial role, and the same goes for Onyewu. Hayes' tactical know-how makes her as qualified as anyone employed by U.S. Soccer to establish the right stylistic profile for the next USMNT coach, especially with the spirit of continuity in mind. Pochettino's track record with the U.S. team was mixed but at its best, his high-intensity, attack-minded approach suited the player pool really well and continues to do so. Hayes, a tactical pragmatist who prioritized attack-minded teams herself with Chelsea and the USWNT, will be more than able to help match candidates to the player pool they will spend the next several years working with. Hayes admitted as much on Wednesday when addressing the topic for the first time.

It has been revealed that "I work really closely with J.T. in particular and even more so with Dan as we're growing to develop the American soccer movement and J.T. asked if I would be involved as a technical voice, to be involved with the process and I feel confident in the group of people that have been put together to create a thorough process to select the next men's national team coach," she said. "My role is merely to support that through a technical lens, knowing I do this job, albeit with the women's team, and that I've coached for a number of years and can offer some of that insight into the application of what to look for and why and like I said, I feel confident in the group that are being put together. I think it'll be a very thorough process. I think that's the most vital part of it and like I said, I feel very embedded in what we're doing with the federation so it doesn't feel unusual to me so, like I've said many times, let's build off the good work that Mauricio has done. I think that's the important part and let's get it right.".

In a recent development, that's especially true considering the fact that there are very few slam-dunk candidates to replace Pochettino. Pep Guardiola, months into a sabbatical after a decade with Manchester City, is an obvious target for U.S. Soccer but it is entirely unclear how interested he would be in the vacancy. If he's out of the running, the list of contenders with genuine international appeal dwindles quickly but it does not necessarily mean the list of worthy candidates vanishes with Guardiola. The hiring committee will need to be strategic in that case, both in terms of creating a list of contenders and then narrowing them down over the interview process, Hayes providing an notable perspective along the way.

Sources indicate that the jobs of the USMNT and the USWNT head coaches are hardly apples-to-apples but even then, one will still have an acute idea of what the other's job entails. There is inherent value in having a coach help in the process of hiring another coach, since they hold such singular positions – they are often treated as the be-all, end-all when it comes to their team's success, fairly or otherwise. She can also speak to the cadence of national teams, which varies greatly from the club game where coaches essentially work with their players every day during a long season.

Recent findings suggest that "Everyone is aware of the major differences between coaching at the club level and international level, and the main difference is just time on the field and time with your players," Hayes told CBS Sports earlier this year when asked about Pochettino. "Every international coach would love to have more time with their team, but that's not the nature of the international calendar and it's something I know we both had to get used to and are still getting used to … I stated a few times that it's almost like we are grandparents. We get to see the players for a week or so and then we send them back to their parents, which is their clubs.".

Outside of her tactical expertise, though, Hayes represents U.S. Soccer's ambitious turn in recent years as much as Pochettino does. She was hired because of her reputation as a serial winner at Chelsea, where she won eight league titles and seven cups. She continued the trend in short order with the USWNT – two months after officially starting in the role, she won Olympic gold at the Paris Games in 2024. U.S. Soccer has equally ambitious goals for the men's team, though the timeline will understandably be longer for that program. They continue to target the USMNT's first World Cup quarterfinal appearance since 2002 but in between, they also hope to medal in the Olympics' men's soccer event, which is contested by U-23 teams, for the first time when the Games come to Los Angeles in 2028. More than many at the federation, Hayes has experience with the intangibles it takes to reach those heights and that's exactly why she was hired in the first place. It also reflects what U.S. Soccer's executives are looking for in the next USMNT head coach.

"The most notable characteristic is someone with ambition that matches ours, which is high and so when you have, then, that high shared ambition, then you look for the experience, the talent, the understanding that accompanies that ambition," Helfrich mentioned.

Industry observers note that beyond that, though, Hayes in particular has an idea of what the USMNT job might entail. She is the best of both worlds – she began her coaching career in the U.S. two decades ago and has a deep understanding of the American soccer landscape, but made a name for herself in her native England and can also bring a useful outsider's perspective. There is no perfect equivalent to Hayes waiting for the USMNT job since no coach with experience in the American game has truly broken into the top tiers of the sport just yet, the federation likely to settle for one or the other. Hayes' understanding of both orbits, though, makes her an crucial guiding force along the way. She might be the only qualified person to answer how much to weigh the insider's perspective with the accomplished outsider's point of view when looking for the next USMNT head coach, in large part because she is the only person who boasts an equal share of it.

Hayes' expertise alone means she will be as valuable a sounding board as any, to the point that it's hard to minimize her ability to offer input down to one or two straightforward things. There is one more thing Hayes might have that no one at U.S. Soccer does – easy access to some of the most notable coaches in the game.

In a recent development, over the course of her successful 12-year tenure at Chelsea, Hayes became one of the most respected coaches in England. She became the first woman to win the Football Writers Association's Tribute Award in 2024 shortly before leaving England for the U.S., and has earned the praise of many of her counterparts in the men's game along the way. Out of anyone at U.S. Soccer, Hayes might actually have the most compelling list of phone numbers in her contacts. She has noted Sir Alex Ferguson, a coaching legend if there ever was one after his storied 27-year tenure at Manchester United, calls her "from time to time." Hayes has been in touch with a handful of her contemporaries over the years, including those who have been on U.S. Soccer's radar at one point or another. In her 2024 book, "A Completely Different Game," Hayes said she heard from Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp after having an emergency hysterectomy because of endometriosis in 2022. The pair "sent me long messages, expressing deeply felt emotions," as did Graham Potter and David Moyes.

The rolodex is a covetable one, if ex-U.S. Soccer sporting director Matt Crocker can serve as an example. His greatest accomplishments during his three-year spell, which came to an end in April when he took a similar role with the Saudi Arabian Football Federation, were hiring Hayes and Pochettino. He had previously worked with Pochettino at Southampton a decade earlier, which made U.S. Soccer's approach easier when discussions started. Hayes' value exceeds her ability to hand her bosses a phone number but it is unlikely to go unnoticed at U.S. Soccer, who clearly understands the expertise she would bring to the search in a variety of ways.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cesc Fabregas feels Como really made a Champions League statement in their 1-0 victory over AEK Athens, and jokes that they can ‘sell Luis Milla for €20m in January’ after his goal.

The Lariani struggled to break down AEK Athens at the Stadio Sinigaglia this evening, especially after Lucas Da Cunha drilled a penalty off target in the first half.

Also hitting the woodwork a couple of times, they eventually found the winner thanks to a Luis Milla curler into the far top corner from outside the box.

“It is a victory that was notable for us, because the level of the Champions League is very high and demanding,” Fabregas told Sky Sport Italia.

In a recent development, “Whether we won or not today, we proved that this team does not struggle to raise the bar when the match takes on a different context. In our five games, we were always competitive, and the most vital thing I wanted to see this season was that.

“The results are going our way and we need to keep going. Serie A remains the most key thing for us, but I cannot deny that it is truly wonderful to experience Champions League nights at the Sinigaglia.”.

Milla got the only goal of the game, and his path to Como was not an easy one, as it took several attempts to finally sign the midfielder.

“We signed him for €6m, maybe we’ll sell him in January for €20m,” smiled Fabregas with Milla waiting nearby for his interview.

“No, I’m kidding, he’s a great player, has had a high level for a long time, his career saw him constantly improve and now he has the kind of character and experience, he is above all a strong presence in the locker room.”.

The Lariani ran a few risks late on too against AEK Athens, so Fabio Capello in the Sky Sport Italia studio asked if Fabregas was worried by their fitness levels in the final 20 minutes?

It has been revealed that “I am always worried! I don’t have your experience to be calm in these situations! The Champions League is of such a level that you can pay for any tiny mistake,” replied the coach.

“The truth is, there aren’t many of us, because there were eight players missing today due to injury and the UEFA squad list limitations, so I think for the first time in my career I only made three substitutions today.

“I did like the character of the squad, the mentality and hunger. Obviously, there are always things to improve, but I liked the approach.”.

This success means Como have won four of their five Champions League games so far this season, losing only 3-2 away to Feyenoord, and have practically guaranteed at least a spot in the play-offs.

#94355. Build for the future climate — or waste trillions of dollars
